📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that starburst Data Inc.
  • Context Studio collects business definitions from existing data catalogs, business intelligence tools, metric stores and documents, making them available alongside data when AI agents respond to prompts.
  • The newly introduced capability addresses a problem the company encountered as customers began deploying its Aida natural-language data assistant in production environments, mentioned Starburst co-founder and Chief Executive Justin Borgman.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 08:00 EST / NOVEMBER 18 2026.

Sources indicate that starburst Data Inc. is expanding its data federation platform into business context management with the introduction of Context Studio, a new capability designed to help artificial intelligence agents produce more accurate and trustworthy answers from information distributed across enterprise systems.

Context Studio collects business definitions from existing data catalogs, business intelligence tools, metric stores and documents, making them available alongside data when AI agents respond to prompts. The system is intended to eliminate conflicting definitions that can cause AI agents to produce incorrect results.

The newly introduced capability addresses a problem the company encountered as customers began deploying its Aida natural-language data assistant in production environments, mentioned Starburst co-founder and Chief Executive Justin Borgman.

“We’ve found that as you get into production, the biggest concern is context because you need to trust the answers the agent gives back,” he remarked.

In a recent development, the challenge is particularly acute in large organizations where different departments may use different definitions of common business metrics, such as revenue or active customers. Without a consistent understanding of those terms, AI models can produce plausible but inaccurate answers.

“When those definitions conflict, the [large language model] doesn’t know any better; it’s just going to guess,” Borgman said. “That’s what leads to bad answers and an erosion of trust.”.

Industry observers note that context Studio builds on Starburst’s existing data products architecture, which allows organizations to create curated views spanning multiple data sources. Those products incorporate business definitions, metadata and access controls that can be applied consistently when agents retrieve information.

Unlike conventional semantic layers that require organizations to consolidate definitions within a single platform, Context Studio federates existing definitions without requiring customers to move or rebuild their underlying data.

Recent findings suggest that built-in approval workflows resolve conflicting definitions, and a feedback mechanism is provided through which agents can propose improvements. Human reviewers approve changes before regression testing checks their impact on other queries.

Borgman characterized the expansion as an evolution of Starburst’s longstanding strategy of querying distributed data without centralizing it.

Sources indicate that “We think context is going to live everywhere, just like we think data will live in multiple places,” he said. “Our approach treats [context] as a first-class principle in our design.”.

It has been revealed that starburst hasn’t yet disclosed quantitative evidence of Context Studio’s impact on AI accuracy or productivity. The tech giant mentioned it is collecting benchmark data from private preview customers.

The organization is also emphasizing traceability to increase confidence in AI-generated answers. Context Studio records which data sources agents access, the SQL queries they generate and the information used to produce responses. Access controls remain attached to underlying data products.

“Context is going to increase the probability of a good answer, but there’s also a need to trace how it got to that answer,” Borgman said.

It has been revealed that an agent can interview domain experts to capture business knowledge and convert it into draft data products. Starburst is also extending its Aida data assistant to answer questions across multiple data products and introducing an agent that automatically generates dashboards.

Industry observers note that other platform enhancements include Mission Control for monitoring usage and costs, automated Apache Iceberg maintenance, a bring-your-own-cloud deployment option and graphics processing unit-accelerated querying. Starburst claims its recently introduced Torin query engine delivers up to sevenfold performance improvements in organization benchmarks.

According to recent reports, context Studio is available in private preview for Starburst Galaxy and Starburst Enterprise. A public preview is planned for January, with general availability expected in the first quarter of 2027. Pricing hasn’t been finalized.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 08:56 EST / NOVEMBER 18 2026.

Universities racing to build AI infrastructure are learning that raw compute changes the pace of science itself, from molecular discovery to materials engineering.

Industry observers note that AI and high-performance computing are converging, and campus technology leaders are now building like cloud operators. The Texas A&M University System is standing up two major clusters for researchers across its 12 universities and eight state agencies, according to Vince Kellen (pictured), chief information officer of The Texas A&M University System.

Recent findings suggest that “A lot of it is going to be related to molecules, molecular discovery, and the size of these computers lets researchers go through their research program in a fraction of the time. What would normally take five months now gets done in a week,” Kellen said. “That’s a massive deal for the scientists. It lets them do more exploration more frequently.”.

Kellen spoke with theCUBE’s Rebecca Knight and Gemma Allen at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how the system’s supercomputing clusters are speeding up molecular discovery, the security and operational demands of running them, and the convergence of AI and supercomputing. (* Disclosure below.).

In a recent development, the system’s VISION supercomputer, an Nvidia Corp. DGX H200 SuperPOD, ranked No. 66 on the June 2026 Top500 list, making it the most powerful university supercomputer in the U.S. — with a second cluster on the way, according to Kellen. The Texas A&M Engineering Experiment Station selected Dell Technologies Inc. to build IGNITE, a platform running Advanced Micro Devices Inc. GPUs in an Equinix Inc. data center in Dallas. With some research tied to highly secure federal contracts, protection tops the policy agenda.

According to recent reports, “On the policy side, our main concern is security. Are we doing this in a secure way?” Kellen mentioned. “Are we vetting the employees who are coming into the platform to make sure that they’re properly credentialed to come in?”.

According to recent reports, texas A&M is working through those access questions as it brings more computing power to researchers across the system, but faster molecular discovery is only the first payoff. Materials engineering, fluid dynamics and other engineering disciplines are next in line, and the system has no prepares to slow its buildout, according to Kellen.

“We already know that AI and supercomputing are one and the same,” he stated. “That trajectory is going to continue in Texas for some time.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"Real Housewives of Beverly Hills" star Dorit Kemsley has revealed she has moved into a newly introduced property after she and her estranged husband, PK Kemsley, were "ordered" to list their longtime Los Angeles mansion following a prolonged legal dispute during which the businessman admitted they were experiencing a "financial crisis.".

While attending the Maison D’Or cocktail launch at The Sun Rose West Hollywood, Dorit told Page Six that she and her children, Jagger, 12, and Phoenix, 10, have found a new place to call home.

“As everyone knows, we were going to court to be evicted by a certain date, which is pretty crummy, but I did find another house. The kids and I are moving into a upcoming home imminently. Fresh beginnings, fresh start. We are all welcoming it," she told the outlet.

Dorit, 50, and PK, 58, are embroiled in a contentious divorce that has been exacerbated by significant monetary woes, including the looming threat of foreclosure on their $7 million Encino, CA, home.

In July, PK requested a judge allow him to sell the property while accusing the reality TV star of leaving their children with her parents in Florida—while providing no information about when she aims to return to the U.S., while he has been left to fight for their home alone.

PK alleged that Dorit was gone for a "minimum of three weeks," per court documents seen by the Newly introduced York Post, stating that her "extended trip" demonstrates her "prioritization of personal travel over addressing the urgent financial crisis facing [their] family home.".

In August, TMZ reported that PK's wish was granted after a judge ordered the sale of the six-bedroom, 10-bathroom Los Angeles abode, while noting that the TV personality had to move out by November.

It has been revealed that according to the outlet, a hearing was held on Aug. 26, when PK alleged that Dorit had not been paying the mortgage on the home.

Meanwhile, Dorit, who is being represented by lawyer Samantha Spector, claimed that PK should be paying the bills, adding that he has enough money to cover the debt as well.

The back and forth between the acrimonious exes continued when PK accused Dorit of delaying the home's listing, while she alleged that he had refused to sign an agreement with celebrity real estate agent Zach Goldsmith of The Agency, whom Dorit remarked she hired to help market the property.

Industry observers note that goldsmith has loose ties to the "Real Housewives of Beverly Hills" world. Not only does he work for Kyle Richards' estranged husband, Mauricio Umansky, he is also expecting a baby with the reality TV star's daughter Farrah Aldjufrie.

Neither PK nor Dorit will be able to delay the sale any longer after a judge determined that the property must be listed, with Goldsmith as the agent, while also ruling that PK should become a manager of the LLC through which they bought the dwelling to ensure a swift sale.

The judge also ruled that Dorit will have to cover the cost of utilities, as well as the past-due amounts.

In a recent development, meanwhile, PK was ordered to pay the mortgage until Dorit moves out. However, he will be reimbursed for all the payments made using any profits from the sale.

According to recent reports, the businessman will also get back the funds he put into the home following their split. The judge denied his request for sanctions.

It marked the latest in what has been a very ugly separation battle between the two reality TV stars.

Just last month, Dorit came under fire from PK when she jetted off on a lavish European vacation, during which she celebrated her 50th birthday in true style, enjoying a lavish lunch alongside Hermès executive Michael Coste.

Dorit's European getaway infuriated her estranged spouse, who filed legal documents on July 13 in which he slammed his former partner for taking the trip while they are still going through a "financial crisis.".

It has been revealed that the home has come close to hitting the foreclosure auction block in recent months. However, each planned sale was postponed, according to reports—although PK's legal team noted in its filing that the risk of their losing the dwelling has "escalated" significantly.

He further claimed in the filing that he stopped the property from falling into foreclosure after splashing out $300,000.

PK alleged that Dorit has not made any mortgage payments, despite raking in a substantial income from "The Real Housewives of Beverly Hills" and spending what he estimates to be $1 million on luxury getaways and designer clothing.

PK argued that she has put her travel intends ahead of the family's financial troubles, requesting that the court allow him to move forward with selling the property.

Dorit filed for divorce from PK in 2025 after 10 years of marriage, citing "irreconcilable differences.".

At the time, she asked the judge to award her sole custody of their kids, in addition to spousal support.

The filing came just one day after PK was photographed sharing a kiss with Shana Wall.

One month after Dorit filed for divorce, PK requested joint custody of their children, while also waiving his right to spousal support and asking the court to do the same for Dorit's plea.

Sources indicate that they unveiled their separation in May 2024 in a joint statement: "We have had our struggles over the last few years and continue to work through them as two people who love each other and share two amazing children together. We have made the mutual and difficult decision to take some time apart and reevaluate our relationship while we prioritize our children.”.

Dorit and PK purchased their sprawling Encino abode for $6.48 million in 2019, according to records, and have since made several attempts to sell it, beginning in September 2020, when they listed the property for $9.5 million.

They reduced their asking price to $7.99 million a few weeks later, before whipping the home off the market altogether.

It was relisted for the same price in April 2021, but once again vanished from the market within a matter of weeks.

The couple have made substantial upgrades to the home since buying it—and have also proudly showcased the property in numerous episodes of their hit Bravo show.

Ahmed Barakat is a journalist and copywriter based in Georgia with a growing focus on blockchain technology, DeFi, AI, privacy, digital assets, and fintech innovation.

It has been revealed that the CryptoNews editorial team is composed of seasoned writers specializing in cryptocurrency and blockchain technology. Their expertise ensures comprehensive, accurate, and insightful content for...

In a recent development, hackers have turned some of the world’s most recognizable websites into potential crypto theft traps after compromising a third-party platform used by 178 major organizations. The attack injected malicious JavaScript through Optimizely, a website experimentation platform trusted by companies including BBC, Zoom, CNN, HSBC, Salesforce, IKEA, and crypto hardware wallet maker Ledger.

Visitors could unknowingly load malware simply by opening an affected webpage, and the consequences go far beyond stolen browsing data. The malicious code can replace crypto wallet addresses copied to the clipboard, redirecting payments straight into attackers’ wallets. Security researchers have already identified $7,040 in crypto received by wallets linked to the campaign.

🚨 BREAKING: Ledger and 177 other major organizations, including Zoom, CNN, and Salesforce, were affected by a massive JavaScript attack.The malware stole cryptocurrency, payment card details, and user data, while also targeting iPhones with exploit kits.

According to recent reports, the investigation by cybersecurity firm Report URI identified 188 infected JavaScript snippets belonging to 178 organizations after examining 1,611 Optimizely scripts. The malware operated through trusted website infrastructure, making the attack particularly dangerous. Rather than breaking into every firm’s servers individually, attackers injected malicious code into Optimizely customer projects.

Affected websites continued loading JavaScript through Optimizely’s legitimate content delivery network. Visitors had little reason to suspect that a familiar website was serving malicious instructions. This is a dangerous clipboard hijacking mechanism.

The malware searched webpages for crypto wallet addresses and replaced legitimate destinations with addresses controlled by attackers. It could also intercept copied addresses, meaning someone browsing an affected website could potentially paste a fraudulent wallet address elsewhere.

The attack targeted several major crypto networks, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, TRON, and Litecoin.

Recent findings suggest that A victim could believe they were sending funds to an exchange, another wallet, or a friend. Instead, the transaction could land directly in an attacker’s wallet.

It has been revealed that report URI identified $7,040 in receipts across attacker-controlled wallets by November 16. The funds included Bitcoin, Litecoin, Ethereum, TRON, and stablecoins.

Discover: The Best Token Presales.

The scale of the incident raises questions about how much trust businesses place in third-party website services. The affected organizations span several industries, including banking, technology, media, retail, and crypto.

It has been revealed that HSBC was among the financial institutions affected, alongside Equifax and other major organizations. BBC, CNN, Fox News, Zoom, Salesforce, GitLab, IKEA, and Air France-KLM also appeared in Report URI’s investigation.

Ledger’s inclusion makes the incident particularly concerning for crypto consumers. The tech giant is known for its hardware wallets, which help customers store private keys away from internet-connected devices. However, the incident demonstrates how threats can reach users through ordinary browsing activity, outside the hardware wallet itself.

Recent findings suggest that the malicious campaign also contained capabilities targeting Apple devices. Researchers identified exploit infrastructure associated with Coruna and DarkSword, two iOS exploit kits designed to target vulnerabilities in iPhones and iPads.

This means the operation was not limited to stealing crypto or payment information. It also carried tools capable of targeting mobile devices through malicious webpage content.

Optimizely confirmed that attackers exploited a vulnerability in its Experimentation account signup flow to inject malicious JavaScript into customer projects. The firm said it blocked access to the vulnerable pathway, deployed a fix, removed injected code, revoked active tokens, and reset access for affected accounts.

It has been revealed that earlier today, Optimizely identified and contained a security incident affecting some Optimizely Web Experimentation customers. The vulnerable path is blocked, the injected code was removed, and customers have been contacted directly. Updates: https://t.co/ptZHZviIeC.

However, the incident raises serious questions about third-party website security. Report URI’s investigation found that even Optimizely’s own websites carried the malicious code. Researchers also observed the attacker rebuilding the malware 26 times during the campaign, adding capabilities and additional cryptocurrency wallets.

Most infected snippets were subsequently cleaned up, with Report URI finding only one remaining infected snippet in its final November 16 sweep.

In a recent development, but the financial damage and potential exposure remain difficult to measure. Researchers have identified crypto receipts, but the number of affected visitors, compromised payment cards, and exposed browser sessions remains unknown.

In a recent development, the bigger problem is that website visitors rarely know which third-party scripts are running behind the pages they trust. A familiar banking website, news outlet, or crypto platform can become an unexpected entry point for malicious code without its visitors noticing anything unusual.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 09:00 EST / NOVEMBER 18 2026.

Governance platform provider OneTrust LLC today announced its Fall ’26 Release, a set of platform updates mentioned to bring governance into the workflows where business decisions are made.

Building on OneTrust CORIE, a shared intelligence layer for governing artificial intelligence agents introduced at the tech giant’s TrustWeek conference in September, the release covers AI visibility, privacy, consent and third-party risk management.

Sources indicate that leading the list of updates is a revised AI inventory, which is designed to reflect changes across a customer’s environment on a continuous basis. According to OneTrust, the change is needed because many organizations running complex networks of AI systems and agents have only limited visibility into how those systems operate. Model associations, potential matches and deprecation indicators from providers are now pulled into the inventory from a curated library of foundation models.

In a recent development, relationships among AI systems, models, agents, projects, risks, controls and workflows can be explored through an interactive AI lineage view. AI performance and operational dashboards, added in the release, bring usage, associated risk, evaluation coverage, outbound personally identifiable information discovery and token consumption into one summary.

Ryan Karlin, vice president of product management at OneTrust, noted knowing which AI systems are in the business “is just the starting point.” According to Karlin, teams also need visibility into the activity and dependencies of those systems “alongside the privacy and third-party risks they already manage.”.

In a recent development, on the third-party risk side, a workflow rule that debuts a risk assessment can now trigger OneTrust’s Deep Research AI skill. The in-depth research report that the skill compiles from public data sources is then used to answer the assessment questionnaire. OneTrust claims the integration can cut the time needed to complete a third-party risk assessment from weeks to minutes.

Drawing on previous assessments and supplier documentation, the company’s expanded AI Document Scanning and Inventory Response Analysis features can now also answer questions about the business engagement tied to a third party.

Sources indicate that for privacy teams, the release adds protections against automated abuse of data subject request web forms. Growing volumes of those automated requests are straining team workloads, according to OneTrust. To filter out the abuse, enhanced CAPTCHA options now work alongside cross-site request forgery token controls to block suspicious submissions.

In the company’s consent management platform, navigation, configuration, scanning, publishing and geolocation management have also been brought into a single workflow under a modernized interface.

It has been revealed that rounding out the release are reporting updates. Enhanced assessment reporting and application programming interfaces are stated to give privacy teams more insight into what drives risk scores. Upcoming risk hierarchy visualizations, which show how individual risks across business units aggregate into enterprise risk categories, are aimed at helping teams prioritize risk treatment.

OneTrust is sharing availability details for the Fall ’26 Release through an overview webinar.

OneTrust has raised $1.13 billion to date, including $150 million in 2023 at a valuation of $4.5 billion. Investors in the manufacturer include Insight Partners LP, Coatue Management, Technology Crossover Ventures LP, SoftBank Vision Fund 2 LP, Franklin Resources Inc., Generation Investment Management LLP and Sands Capital Management.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that A fresh metro-by-metro analysis from Realtor.com® reveals where buyers can still find a starter home. These options have felt increasingly scarce as rising prices and climbing mortgage rates create challenges for many would-be buyers.

According to recent reports, according to research, the national share of starter homes in active inventory fell from 38.1% in August 2019 to 36.2% in August 2026. During that same period, starter home prices rose 30.8%, from about $260,000 to $340,000.

However, some cities are bucking this trend, and Portland, OR, has seen an encouraging uptick in starter homes in recent years.

A starter home is defined as a property priced at roughly 80% of a metro's median list price, capturing the relative affordability of an area's lower-end market. These homes are typically smaller and less expensive, making them accessible to a first-time buyer or a household with an Income at or below the local median.

In the Portland-Vancouver, OR-WA, metro area, the share of starter homes has shown positive growth. The share was 28.0% in 2019 and dipped slightly to 27.8% in 2022 before rising to 32.0% in 2026.

This represents a total increase of +4.0 percentage points since 2019, signaling growing opportunity for buyers in the market.

For those deciding between renting or buying, current data suggests renting is the more affordable path for now. A July Rent Report found that the cost of buying a starter home in the 50 largest metros was $858 higher per month than renting one. This financial advantage to renting holds true across all 50 of the largest metros.

In the Portland-Vancouver, OR-WA, market, the median rent cost was $1,606 as of July 2026.

This figure represents a 1.60% decrease year-over-year, making an apartment an even more financially sound choice while saving for a down payment. Prospective buyers can use a rent vs. buy calculator to weigh their options.

Tech Report: Tesorai raises $5.3M to feed starving AI models with biological data and accelerate drug discovery

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Drug researchers and medical laboratories generate massive volumes of biological data every single day, yet somehow the artificial intelligence models designed to speed up drug discovery are still starved of useful information.
  • It’s a strange paradox, but a startup called Tesorai Inc.
  • The round included Perplexity Fund, IQT, South Central Ventures, Upcoming Stack Ventures, NextGen Venture Partners, f7 Ventures, VitalStage Ventures and ZAKA participating.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 09:00 EST / NOVEMBER 18 2026.

Drug researchers and medical laboratories generate massive volumes of biological data every single day, yet somehow the artificial intelligence models designed to speed up drug discovery are still starved of useful information.

It’s a strange paradox, but a startup called Tesorai Inc. believes it has the solution after raising $5.3 million in seed funding today.

The round included Perplexity Fund, IQT, South Central Ventures, Upcoming Stack Ventures, NextGen Venture Partners, f7 Ventures, VitalStage Ventures and ZAKA participating. With its completion, Tesorai has now raised $8 million in total, and will use that money to try to accelerate AI-driven scientific discovery by digging deeper into existing datasets to surface the deeply buried insights that human researchers have missed.

It has been revealed that biological data covers a broad spectrum spanning genetic sequences to protein measurements, and metabolomic processes to cellular imaging. This information is extremely valuable to drug researchers, because it serves as the primary fuel for training advanced AI models that can predict disease pathways and identify new therapies.

Industry observers note that AI-accelerated drug discovery is seen as one of the most promising use cases for this technology, but it hasn’t yet managed to change the world in the same way that generative AI has done. Why not? Because researchers still don’t have nearly enough of it, which limits the accuracy of the best models they’ve come up with so far.

According to recent reports, to combat this scarcity of biological data, tech giants including OpenAI Group PBC, Google LLC’s DeepMind, Meta Platforms Inc., Isomorphic Labs Inc. and others are spending billions of dollars to generate more of it, but Tesorai’s co-founders Charlie Kim, Melissa Miao and Peter Cimermancic believe it’s also possible to do more with less.

To that end, Tesorai’s goal is to unlock the biological data that researchers already have access to. Rather than using the summarized findings available in published research papers and clinical studies, it uses AI to analyze raw spectrometry data generated by lab instruments.

Its platform consists of Tesorai Search, which rapidly ingests and analyzes terabytes of data from different sources. There’s also Tesorai Chat, which is used by scientists to ask questions of biological datasets in plain English. And there’s Tesorai Trove, a curated catalog of thousands of publicly available datasets and studies.

In a recent development, those three components work together to process the raw instrument data from both new and historical lab studies and experiments, before analyzing it thoroughly to try to surface insights that were missed by their authors. By using those insights, Tesorai believes it can train more accurate AI models for drug discovery and therapy research.

“Life science R&D is accelerating and becoming increasingly autonomous, which makes it more notable to extract as much insight as possible from every experiment,” Chief Scientific Officer Kim explained. “Tesorai does this for a lab’s newly introduced data and for thousands of published studies, and the gains compound as each experiment builds on the last. Ultimately, this will help the industry to develop better medicines faster.”.

Recent findings suggest that the startup points to a number of discoveries it has unearthed that were missed by previous studies. In one example, Tesorai reprocessed and re-crunched the data from five studies of the human brain in Alzheimer’s disease-afflicted patients. Through its analysis, it identified a key Alzheimer’s biomarker called p-tau217 that was missed in all five of the studies. Tesorai ran the analysis to test an Alzheimer’s blood panel published in JAMA Neurology in August, and it posted its findings as a preprint later that month.

In another example, Tesorai illustrated how it was able to accelerate AI model training by adding protein data to a small single-cell AI model, enabling it to beat larger RNA-only models, including one with 40 times more parameters, on multiple benchmarks.

Miao, who’s Tesorai’s chief executive officer, said basically every scientific study produces much more data than what’s reported by its authors. Moreover, most of those studies are never revisited. “Our platform reclaims the value of experiments that have already been done and amplifies each new experiment with the relevant evidence that already exists,” she said.

Industry observers note that tesorai’s early success has paved the way for its initial traction, and it has already established partnerships with the MD Anderson Cancer Center, Fresh York University and the Michael J. Fox Foundation. With the funds from today’s round, it will try to secure more partnerships with the life sciences industry, catalog more public studies and expand its platform to cover other molecular data beyond proteins and genomes.

Sources indicate that perplexity Fund General Partner Joanna Lee Shevelenko said it’s clear that AI can dramatically accelerate scientific research, and that’s why it needs as much high-quality experimental data as possible. “Tesorai is building the infrastructure to make that data usable at scale, giving scientists and AI systems a stronger foundation for advancing research,” she said.

  • According to recent reports, brokerage expansion stretched from the Caribbean to the West Coast in recent days, as firms moved into fresh markets and picked up agents and teams from other companies.
  • According to recent reports, eXp Realty picked up a Tampa Bay brokerage and a Cincinnati-area team that spent 20 years with REMAX.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Engel & Völkers announced an Aruba shop, Realty of America entered San Diego, and eXp Realty added a Tampa Bay brokerage and an Ohio team.

According to recent reports, brokerage expansion stretched from the Caribbean to the West Coast in recent days, as firms moved into fresh markets and picked up agents and teams from other companies. Engel & Völkers is headed to Aruba, where it looks to open a shop in April 2027, and Realty of America reached California with Zandra Ulloa and 12 of her Team Z Realty agents in San Diego.

According to recent reports, eXp Realty picked up a Tampa Bay brokerage and a Cincinnati-area team that spent 20 years with REMAX. Baird & Warner brought on Oak Park, Illinois, boutique Beyond Properties, and Dane Briggs teamed up with Phil Sexton at HomeSmart’s NEXT team. IRES MLS welcomed back a former staffer to run operations, and Howard Hanna Portside added an agent in Massachusetts.

Engel & Völkers expanded into Aruba with license partners Zobaida Akkari and Richard Franken, Aruba-based entrepreneurs with backgrounds in real estate, luxury sales, hospitality and tourism. The shop is projected to open in April 2027 at L.G. Smith Blvd. 330 in Palm Beach and will serve clients across the island, according to the company.

“Aruba is a compelling addition to the network’s growing presence in the Caribbean,” Stuart Siegel, president and CEO of Engel & Völkers Americas, remarked in a statement.

Sources indicate that realty of America entered California with Zandra Ulloa and 12 Team Z Realty agent partners in San Diego. Ulloa has generated more than $4.2 billion in sales volume over her 13-year career, and Team Z peaked at 72 agents and $589 million in annual volume, according to the company. Agent-owned ROA, founded in September 2024, says it has more than 3,900 agents across 26 markets.

“People around me may see what I am giving up, but I see what I am making room for,” Ulloa stated in a statement.

Rene Carpena and Dana Carpena moved Florida’s 1st Choice Realty, their independent Greater Tampa Bay brokerage, to eXp Realty, where it now operates as 1st Choice Collective. The group brings more than 70 agents and support staff and recorded more than 325 transactions and $60 million in sales volume in 2025, according to the company.

Jon Bowling also brought his 17-person team in Mason, Ohio, to eXp after 20 years with RE/MAX. eXp Realty is the core subsidiary of AGNT Inc.

Industry observers note that baird & Warner added Beyond Properties, a boutique brokerage in Oak Park, Illinois, whose dozen agents will operate as Beyond Properties Group. Owner and designated managing broker Erica Cuneen, who founded the firm almost 20 years ago, will co-lead the group with team leader Cynthia Howe Gajewski. The group joins Baird & Warner’s Oak Park office and keeps its Marion Street location.

“This partnership will allow me to simplify the operational side of the business and spend more time doing what I love, which is focusing on our agents and clients,” Cuneen said in a statement.

According to recent reports, dane Briggs, an Arizona real estate veteran, partnered with Phil Sexton, founder of HomeSmart’s NEXT team, in a leadership role focused on agent workflows and AI integrations. Briggs has worked as a designated broker and title executive, founded referral brokerage Roosted and led expansion initiatives at Homie. He has also served as an Inman Ambassador.

“Before long, we weren’t just talking about what Phil was building. We were talking about what we could build together,” Briggs mentioned in a statement.

IRES MLS, which serves Northern Colorado and parts of the Front Range, rehired Samantha Ewing as director of operations. Ewing spent 13 years at IRES as a projects manager and quality assurance tester before leaving in 2018, and she has more than 20 years of experience in MLS operations and real estate technology.

“Having Samantha return to IRES is an exciting opportunity for our team and the local industry we serve,” CEO Julie Dahl said in a statement.

In a recent development, howard Hanna Portside Real Estate Group added Melissa Winter, an agent with nearly 15 years of experience who focuses on first-time homebuyers, to its Massachusetts team in Amesbury. Portside, which has more than 200 agents, entered a strategic partnership with Howard Hanna in 2026, according to the firm.

“What drew me to Portside was the energy, the people, and the opportunity for growth,” Winter said in a statement.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Jumping out of a helicopter into water below, rappelling down a 22-story building, enduring chemical warfare gas exposure — if you’ve never seen Special Forces: World’s Toughest Test, these are just a few of the tasks that must be completed.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jumping out of a helicopter into water below, rappelling down a 22-story building, enduring chemical warfare gas exposure — if you’ve never seen Special Forces: World’s Toughest Test, these are just a few of the tasks that must be completed.

It’s a reality TV show in which celebrities do physical challenges from the actual Special Forces selection process playbook. It’s like a competition show, but there are no eliminations, and no one gets voted off.

It has been revealed that to leave, participants must voluntarily withdraw, be medically withdrawn by a DS (directing staff) due to injury or be dismissed for refusing a direct order. During the final test, the DS ejects those who fail the interrogation or selection test.

It has been revealed that season 5 is set in the Malaysian jungle. It features Candace Cameron Bure, Brandi Glanville, Oliver Hudson, Ruby Rose, George Santos, Bre Tiesi, Matt Barnes, and Mauricio and Alexia Umansky, among others.

At the time that this article was published, Alexia was still in the competition. Mauricio voluntarily withdrew after a rib injury sustained during a hand-to-hand fighting challenge with former NBA player Matt Barnes. Mauricio remarked the injury took two or three months to heal.

The following challenge involved gas, and Mauricio didn’t think his ribs could take it. He said he feared having a bad lung injury in the Malaysian jungle. Alexia agreed with the decision, saying the gas was the “most painful thing” she’d ever experienced in her life.

Inman spoke to Mauricio and Alexia midway through the season about the experience, the latest industry news and what’s next for The Agency.

What follows is the conversation, edited for length and clarity.

It has been revealed that I think for me, 100 percent, the heat. I think I anticipated intense heat and intense humidity, but you don’t know what it’s like until you really feel it … It was so unbearably hot, and in our barracks that we slept in, there was no windows, and when you were inside, you actually couldn’t tell like what was even happening out there. But it was almost like … “Good, let me be locked in this metal box because the outside is crazy.”.

Sources indicate that mauricio: I think for me, it was just the intensity of what a jungle really is. The first day we got there … when we were all showering and waiting to shower, there was a scorpion crawling on my leg, about to go in my boot, which I felt it and took it off just in the nick of time. Because if it went in my boot, it would have stung me, no question, right?

Recent findings suggest that alexia: It’s so hard to choose because literally every single thing was hard. Part of me wanted to say the car rides leading up to each challenge, because we didn’t know what was coming, and it was always so intense in the car. My heart would start pounding … the bottom line is the hardest part is just making sure that your mindset is correct [in] doing all these things and waking up each day and moving forward because that’s really what gets going is just moving forward and choosing to keep on going.

Mauricio: Yeah, I think Alexia nailed it. I mean, for me, it was really all about the little victories. The only way to survive is by looking at small victories, small steps … we used to say just make it to the next meal, just make it to the next day, just make it to tonight.

Recent findings suggest that for me, the hardest part was leaving, was having to voluntarily withdraw. I did not want to have a medical withdrawal, so I didn’t want to go see the doctor and have them withdraw me.

Mauricio: Not one thing for me. What about you, Alexia?

Sources indicate that alexia: No. There’s nothing about this that’s easy.

Alexia: We loved everybody so much. I mean, we still talk all the time, and we still love each other so much. The words of affirmation we all told each other to this day are so special … But I think my first answer would have to be Candace [Cameron] Bure … she’s so strong, and we got looped together for a bunch of things because of our height similarities.

Mauricio: Well, I have to say that the person who surprised me the most was Alexia … the strength of her mind, her strength and what she did was extraordinary.

Sources indicate that alexia: Oh my god, yeah. Are you kidding me? All the time.

Alexia: Definitely thought it was pretty cool. It was an honor to be punched in the chest by DJ Tanner … I actually appreciated very much that she didn’t hold back because I just felt like I was treated like an equal, an individual.

According to recent reports, alexia: I’ve never punched anyone or anything … the second she threw the first punch, I knew she was so much stronger than me. But my goal was to just not fall down. I really didn’t want to fall down, so I was just trying to stay up the entire time. It felt like a fight went on for so long.

According to recent reports, pete Dadds / FOX. ©2026 FOX Media LLC.as.

Alexia: I had zero plans on talking about that while we were there. Before we go into the course, they make you talk to some psychologists … they do ask you before the show, “What’s the worst thing that you’ve ever been through?”.

It has been revealed that and I remember thinking, like, “Are we gonna go there? … That would be so inappropriate. Everything’s in my power, and I’m not gonna go there” … Once I was finally in there, I understood why they asked … you’re stripped down to the very core of you, and you’re tired, and you’re pushing yourself, and you’re emotional, you’re exhausted … And Bre Tiesi, she got emotional, and [she remarked to me] ”I haven’t cried in years. I hate crying.”.

It was really about discovering and repurposing the strength that I always felt that I had, but there was a time that I had felt that I had lost that.

And each night, as I was going to sleep, I just remember thinking to myself, “This is so rewarding, and this is so empowering, and this is so incredible for someone that has gone through what I have” … some people [feel like they] get their voice back. I always felt like I had my voice, but I feel like I got to discover a strength I always knew I had that someone had pushed me to question, and feeling that was just incredibly healing.

Industry observers note that alexia: No, not my parents. I had told two of my sisters before, and then, obviously, I told my dad on the course, and then, before the show aired, I ended up calling my mom and [sister] Portia to tell them because I obviously did not want that to be the first time they read it. And even though I spoke about it on the course, I’m still very, very afraid to tell them afterward, too.

Mauricio: It was extremely difficult … I was just proud of Alexia every single day, every single moment … hearing that story was just another revelation of her conquering and finally talking about something that I wish she never held back … I just wanted to reach out and just hug her. But by the same token, I also wanted to give her space and let her be her in that moment that she was sharing with everybody. So there was like a lot of stuff going through my mind.

There was anger toward this kid that did this … But [watching her let go of it] was beautiful to watch … from my perspective, it was like, “Do I reach over and become a dad and just give her a big hug, or do I let her go through this moment, psychologically speaking, of letting it all come out?”.

And I was just proud of her all the way around.

In hindsight, I love that she was able to share that, get it off her chest with us, with everybody, with the world. I think it’s super powerful.

Pete Dadds / FOX. ©2026 FOX Media LLC.as.

Sources indicate that yes, I live by a lot of different small philosophies. Certainty versus doubt. Momentum is the cure of all fears. All of these are the different things where you just have to move forward, right? In order to accomplish something, you kind of just have to move forward, right? … the moment that I went from being an agent to opening up a brokerage, you jump off the cliff; you hope the parachute catches.

To today … here we are in a really difficult real estate market. I mean, it is not fun out there right now whatsoever. Yet [The Agency is] still growing. We’re still putting money out there. We’re still doing things right. So yeah, to me that’s just a philosophy that I always live by.

In a recent development, mauricio: I don’t know. We’ll just keep going. I really like that show Traitors. I would love to be on that show. That could be a fun one for me, so I’m putting that out into the universe.

Industry observers note that alexia: My dream would be to do a reality TV show with my family … We did Buying Beverly Hills, and we’ve done Real Housewives for like [16] years now. But we’ve never done something all of us together, just us, and I think that’ll be really cool.

In a recent development, mauricio: I’m going to leave that one on the table. If anything, it’s for 2030. There’s still plenty of time to do that and make that decision. But I love LA, and I think I can help LA a lot. I think we live in an amazing city, and if the moment comes, and I’m set up in the right position in the business and I feel like I can actually win, I might do it. But I wouldn’t do it if I didn’t feel like I could actually win.

Mauricio: It’s an absolute mess, what’s going on in our in our in our industry right now, particularly with the listings. My take is, it’s quite simple. I think that there’s a lot of change that’s happening. I believe that it’s somewhere in the middle. Like I do everything.

I believe sellers should have choice, but I believe that we should be sharing those private listings amongst everybody — every agent, every brokerage firm, not just keeping it for themselves. I feel like there’s a lot happening right now in the industry where everybody’s really looking out for themselves: the MLSs, NAR, Compass.

In a recent development, actually, Compass, I think, wants to collaborate, wants to share, but they’re in a major, big fight. But in the meantime, this Clear Cooperation Policy is what is allowing them to keep all the listings to themselves and not share them … The PLS is exactly what that was, and I still think that if Clear Cooperation Policy didn’t pass, it would have been an amazing business to have right now.

Recent findings suggest that mauricio: We are really positioned as the premier luxury brokerage firm outside of Compass right now. They’ve got Sotheby’s, they’ve got Christie’s, they’ve got all of those different brands, and we’re the only independent luxury brokerage firm out there right now.

According to recent reports, so I’m excited to be in that position. Competitors make you better every single day … I’m excited in terms of where we sit, where we stand in a very difficult time; I’m not excited about the market. We really need to do some things to improve it. We’ve had three years of very, very difficult conditions, and it’s going to be very difficult for people to survive. And those that do survive will come out better.

I think we’re in a good position to survive, but we’ve got our work cut out for us over the next year, year and a half. But we’ll continue to grow. We’ll continue to expand, and I’m excited to just be a part of this industry. But man, it’s hard out there right now.

Breaking: Reson8 releases Rumble-2-Flash speech model as a free open-weights download

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that amsterdam-based speech recognition startup Resonate Labs B.V.
  • Designed for fast transcription of prerecorded audio, the 500 million-parameter model supports more than 40 languages.
  • According to the firm, the leading speech models are trained primarily on English, even though only about one in 20 people speak it as a first language.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 09:00 EST / NOVEMBER 18 2026.

Sources indicate that amsterdam-based speech recognition startup Resonate Labs B.V. today released its Rumble-2-Flash transcription model as a free download with open weights.

Designed for fast transcription of prerecorded audio, the 500 million-parameter model supports more than 40 languages. Reson8 is pitching the release at developers and researchers who need speech recognition built for languages other than English.

According to the firm, the leading speech models are trained primarily on English, even though only about one in 20 people speak it as a first language. Specialist terms such as medication names are where accuracy is mentioned to fall furthest once speech moves outside English. Reson8’s models are said to be in production use for meeting notetakers, artificial intelligence receptionists, customer support voice agents, medical transcription and captioning.

Industry observers note that “Generic speech models are built for English and make noticeably more mistakes in other languages,” said co-founder and Chief Executive Raoul Ritter, who started the company with Thomas Kluiters and Jarno Verhagen. “Languages like Dutch, Swedish and German are spoken by millions, yet they’re an afterthought.”.

Reson8 describes Rumble-2-Flash as one of the smallest models on Hugging Face Inc.’s Open ASR Leaderboard. In the manufacturer’s own runs of the leaderboard’s multilingual tests, the model averaged a word error rate of 7.09% across seven languages, including German, French and Dutch. Its average error rate in English is claimed to be about 5%.

Recent findings suggest that on a separate test covering 10 lower-resource languages such as Maltese and Basque, Rumble-2-Flash is said to have posted a mean word error rate of 17.6%. OpenAI Group PBC’s Whisper Large V3 had a mean word error rate of 39.82% on the same test, according to Reson8.

Beyond benchmark sets, Reson8’s models are noted to be trained for noisy settings, including phone-line audio. The real world “doesn’t happen in a recording studio,” said Kluiters, the firm’s head of AI.

In a recent development, today’s open-weights release follows the model’s Nov. 3 debut in Reson8’s application programming interface, a week before the company introduced its flagship Rumble-2 model. Custom vocabulary support, which lets customers add up to 50,000 terms as text without fine-tuning, remains exclusive to Rumble-2.

Hosted on the tech giant’s own graphics processing units in the Netherlands, Reson8’s service is stated to retain no audio or transcripts. The company also claims ISO 27001 certification and compliance with the European Union’s General Data Protection Regulation and the bloc’s AI Act.

Available free under an Apache 2.0 license, Rumble-2-Flash can also be accessed through Reson8’s API at prices starting from €0.01 ($0.001) per hour of audio.

According to recent reports, reson8 raised €5 million ($5.5 million) in pre-seed funding in March. Balderton Capital led the round, with NP-Hard Ventures also participating. Speech is “quickly becoming a default interface across software,” according to James Wise, a partner at Balderton.

Kris Jenner is welcoming the holiday season with a glowing display at her California mansion, where warm white lights outline the gates, hedges, roofline, and doorways.

Recent findings suggest that the reality TV star, 71, shared a look at the decorations in a video posted to Instagram on Nov. 13, giving followers a view of the home’s exterior as the entrance gates opened.

The clip is set to “Somewhere in My Memory,” the instrumental piece associated with the film "Home Alone.".

As the gates move apart, the lights come into view across the landscaping and around the house, creating a bright welcome along the property’s entrance.

“It’s my favorite time of the year!” Jenner wrote in the caption. She described the setup as “the chicest Christmas lights in all the land” and “just magical! I could stare at them all night.”.

The display extends beyond the immediate entrance. Trees, bushes, and other landscaping are also illuminated, making the lights visible throughout the grounds.

The video focuses on the home’s exterior, where the warm white lighting brings attention to the landscaping and the architectural outlines of the mansion.

Jenner’s post arrives as her family begins sharing its holiday decorating for the year.

Her daughter Khloé Kardashian highlighted off the lights at her own Los Angeles home earlier in November.

It has been revealed that thousands of white lights were arranged around the trees, windows, and doors, giving the exterior a gingerbread house-inspired look. Kardashian credited lighting installation company The Christmas Brothers with the work.

The holiday displays have become a recurring part of the Kardashian-Jenner family’s seasonal social media posts.

Last year, Jenner’s daughters Kim and Kourtney Kardashian gave followers a peek at another festive detail at their mother’s home: a bunk room prepared for the grandchildren.

The sleeping area featured several sets of bunk beds dressed with red checked bedspreads, Christmas wreaths, and twinkling lights.

Kourtney described the setup as “magical” in an Instagram Stories post, while Kim shared her own reaction to the room, asking how cute her mother’s bunk bed room was for the children.

Jenner also shared glimpses of the family’s interior holiday decorations in photos from their Christmas Eve celebration in 2025.

The images showed a fireplace dressed with garland and lights, with stockings hanging from the mantel.

A collection of Christmas trees stood beneath the staircase, each dripping in ornaments. The dining table was arranged with red linens, plaid dishes, greenery, and reindeer-inspired candleholders.

This year’s video turns the attention back outside, offering a quick look at the lights welcoming guests to Jenner’s home.

With the gates opening onto illuminated landscaping and the house outlined in white lights, the display gives the family’s holiday season a festive start.

#41697. Latest Update: We keep coaching real estate agents to be salespeople. That was never the job

📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (981 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Inman ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: We keep coaching real estate agents to be salespeople. That was never the job

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (981 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Inman

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • OPINION: Lance Pendleton argues that real estate agents are consultants, not salespeople.
  • Industry observers note that I was the national head of agent development at Compass, and I’ve been in front of more than 30,000 agents since.
  • It has been revealed that the reason is simpler than anybody wants it to be.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

OPINION: Lance Pendleton argues that real estate agents are consultants, not salespeople. Learn what to ask before you pay for a coaching program.

Industry observers note that I was the national head of agent development at Compass, and I’ve been in front of more than 30,000 agents since. I’ve also sold the thing I’m about to take apart, so keep that in mind while you read.

You didn’t fail the program. The program failed you. How come?

It has been revealed that the reason is simpler than anybody wants it to be. Nearly every coaching program in this business teaches professional sales skills to people who are not in sales. We’re consultants, advocates, advisors and educators.

Sources indicate that nobody has ever talked a family into a house they didn’t want to live in. What we do is help people through the largest and most emotional decision of their lives with the least amount of damage. We read a room. We tell someone the truth about their kitchen, and we hold a deal together at 9 p.m. on a Sunday when the buyer’s father has opinions.

Sources indicate that that is not selling. We’re consultants, advocates, advisors and educators. If you can fog a mirror, you can get a license. Very few people can do those four things well, and I’ve yet to see a program that teaches them as a skill set.

This isn’t the coach’s fault. Coaches were trained the same way the rest of us were. Build the database. Reach as many people as you possibly can. Add value, and then add more of it tomorrow.

Industry observers note that there’s a word buried in there that I think is the dumbest one in our industry, and I say that with love. Value.

In a recent development, we all have the same value. Every one of us can pull a comp, open a door, write an offer and get to a closing table. What almost none of us have is a point of differentiation, the thing that tells a consumer specifically what you do for them and why it ought to be you. You can follow “add value” for a decade and stay interchangeable with the other four agents the seller interviewed.

There’s a second reason the homework never gets done: Agents live in two periods of time: now and not now.

Industry observers note that now is the pipe that burst three hours before a closing. Now is the appraisal, the inspection, the client calling at 10:30 p.m. about something that could have been a text. Now is loud, it’s permanent, and it pays this month. Not now is quiet and pays in three years, if at all.

Industry observers note that the trouble is that everything producing long-term income security in this business sits in the not-now column. The National Association of Realtors’ 2026 member profile puts median gross income at $88,500 for agents with 16 years or more in the industry, and $8,000 for agents with two years or less.

According to recent reports, the veterans report a median 49 percent of their business from repeat clients and another 32 percent from referrals. For the newest agents, both of those medians are zero.

Recent findings suggest that somebody will say that’s just arithmetic, that you need a past client before you can have a repeat one. That’s the point. The whole gap is 15 years of relationships, and not one hour of that work feels urgent on a Tuesday. This is a patient business being coached like an impatient one.

It has been revealed that we do something else I think is worse. We coach in a permanent state of enthusiasm. Everything is fabulous; every market is an opportunity; you’re crushing it; this is your year. I call that toxic positivity, and it does real damage. You sit in a hard month with two deals coming apart, you hear all of it, and you quietly conclude the problem must be you.

According to recent reports, what would help is unglamorous. This job burns through five things: prioritization, organization, time management, impulse control and emotional regulation. By Thursday of an ordinary week, most good agents are running low on at least two.

There’s nothing wrong with any of those people. Real support builds bumpers around those five, the same reason a bowling lane for kids has them. You don’t make the gutter disappear by concentrating harder.

Sources indicate that that work means dealing with people as they are, for who they are. Not more, more, more. Not the next great thing. One thing, chosen for that person, small enough to start on a Thursday when everything else has gone sideways.

We haven’t served this business well on that, and I include myself. I’ve sold the four-week cycle. It’s a comfortable thing to sell, because Week 1 always works.

According to recent reports, if you’re picking a program this fall, ask what gets cut. Anybody can hand you 15 things. The one worth paying is the person who tells you which one matters and which 14 you can skip.

It has been revealed that we’re not in sales. We never were. Until the coaching in this business is built for that job, we’ll keep running very good people through programs that leave them feeling like the problem.

Sources indicate that you aren’t the problem. This is still the best time there’s ever been to be a great agent. We just have to stop training you for somebody else’s job.

The views and opinions expressed here are those of the contributor and separate from the Inman newsroom.

In a recent development, lance Pendleton is the founder of Reframe Lab, a coaching and consulting practice for real estate agents, and the former national head of agent development at Compass in Connecticut. Get connected on Instagram.

Strategy, the world's largest corporate Bitcoin (BTC) holder, has sent an key message regarding Bitcoin’s future resistance to quantum computing attacks.

The company, which was co-founded by renowned Bitcoin champion Michael Saylor, recently posted on X that the Bitcoin network can implement new security measures as and when they are needed.

“Quantum-resistant upgrades can be adopted if & when it's needed,” wrote Strategy.

These comments come at a time when the crypto industry is debating whether the rise of quantum computing could, in the long run, threaten Bitcoin’s cryptographic security.

Given that Bitcoin leverages elliptic curve cryptography for transaction security, quantum computing could pose a significant threat to Bitcoin.

A sufficiently powerful quantum computer has the potential to reverse-engineer private keys from exposed public keys. This could give attackers access to the Bitcoin holdings associated with those keys.

At this point, there is no known publicly available quantum computer that can successfully break Bitcoin’s cryptography in this manner.

While speaking at the World Bank in Washington in October, Saylor said that the Bitcoin network would be able to defend itself against any realistic quantum computing threat by coming together and upgrading the software.

Saylor estimated that such an upgrade would take about 90 days once a worldwide consensus is reached on the need for quantum-resistant cryptography.

It has been revealed that saylor also warned against the hasty introduction of fresh cryptography. He reasoned that more complex security measures may themselves introduce weaknesses.

However, the 90-day estimate has come under scrutiny because such a network-wide shift would involve developers agreeing on technical changes and Bitcoin owners moving their funds to new, secure addresses.

Interestingly, Strategy has also initiated efforts aimed at research and development for Bitcoin’s long-term security.

In July, Strategy was part of a group of seven major financial institutions and crypto companies, including BlackRock and Coinbase, that formed the Bitcoin Security Consortium.

In a recent development, the Bitcoin Security Consortium has committed $15 million over three years. One of the areas of focus of the consortium is post-quantum cryptography.

In fact, Bitcoin developers are already working on ways to address the quantum computing problem.

It has been revealed that one of the most prominent proposals is Bitcoin Improvement Proposal 360 (BIP-360). This BIP introduces a new type of transaction output, Pay-to-Merkle-Root (P2MR).

UPDATED 09:28 EST / NOVEMBER 18 2026.

In a recent development, quantum computing is shedding its reputation as speculative as gains in quantum error correction turn fragile machines into reliable ones. For the supercomputing community, which now measures data centers in gigawatts of power, the more pressing question is how quantum fits beside the processors already on the floor.

For years, the field faced a trade-off between speed and reliability, because correcting errors inside a quantum computer slowed it down. That trade-off is fading fast, according to Rajeeb Hazra (pictured), chief executive officer of Quantinuum Inc., which listed on the Nasdaq in June.

“We are now at a stage in 2026 where we have the ability to have tremendous amounts of computation at a very high reliability rate,” Hazra remarked. “Just two weeks ago, we declared we were doing up to a million operations with five errors. To put it in contrast, just two years ago, we were trying to do 1,000 operations with one error. That’s how fast it is.”.

Hazra spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Gemma Allen at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed advances in quantum error correction and how AI and quantum computing work in tandem. (* Disclosure below.).

Recent findings suggest that quantinuum’s 100-qubit Helios system recently set an error-correction record, reaching logical fidelity equivalent to five errors per million operations. The manufacturer builds the full stack, from hardware to developer tools, so customers can model problems such as how a drug ages and loses potency, Hazra explained. That positions quantum less as a rival to AI than as a tool AI will lean on for accurate simulation.

“We see AI and quantum working in tandem, or rather AI using quantum computers,” Hazra said. “I don’t think it’s people using quantum computers; it’s AI programming quantum computers to get the data they need to do what AI does best, which is reasoning and prediction.”.

Recent findings suggest that two cloud service providers have already struck deals with Quantinuum, and most of its use-case customers are commercial companies in pharma, energy, chemicals and financial services, Hazra explained. With quantum error correction maturing, the payoff lies in designing materials that release medicine only where the body needs it.

Recent findings suggest that “My view is in five to seven years max, you’re not going to get a prescription for amoxicillin,” Hazra stated. “You’re going to get a sheet of paper that basically notes this is your pathology. It’ll get matched up at CVS Pharmacy with the available proteins, if you will, and you will get your personalized medicine.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Can AI time savings be measured? Lofty is trying. Plus: $1.65 billion in October proptech funding, Airbnb’s AI travel agent and Zillow Preview in RealScout.

This week’s Inman Tech Roundup covers Lofty’s newly introduced monthly index, which tallies how much time its AI saves agents, a $1.65 billion October for proptech funding, Airbnb’s early-2027 launch window for its AI travel agent and Zillow Preview’s new home inside RealScout.

Sources indicate that lofty is launching the Lofty AI Index for Real Estate, a monthly report tracking how much time its AI tools save real estate agents. The inaugural edition found Lofty AI products, including Lofty Cowork, completed 1.13 million tasks in October, saving real estate agents 131,248 hours.

The index counts tasks Lofty’s AI completed, such as follow-ups, social media posts, homeowner check-ins and CRM updates, then estimates how long each would take an agent to do manually.

Among the findings: 387,824 leads got an AI follow-up text or email; solo agents saved 30 percent of their hours on daily planning; and agents in Michigan saved more time than any other region.

In a recent development, “Every AI vendor touts the time-saving nature of their AI product, but almost none of them show the data to confirm that what they say is true. We decided to cut through the smoke and mirrors around AI results and create measurable clarity with the Lofty AI Index. Each month we’ll put a number to the AI impact, show the calculations and stand behind it,” noted Joe Chen, CEO of Lofty.

The time-saved figures rest on the company’s own estimates of manual task times, and the release doesn’t say how many agents are behind the totals, which makes per-agent impact hard to gauge. Since this is the first edition, there’s no prior month to compare against yet.

Sources indicate that for real estate agents weighing AI tools, Lofty’s index is a step toward the kind of hard numbers the industry has been missing. It gives them a benchmark to press other vendors on when they make time-saving claims.

However, the most useful measure is their own: tracking whether hours freed up by AI actually turn into more conversations, listings and closings.

Note: Lofty is the official AI partner of Inman.

Proptech companies raised about $1.65 billion across 34 funding rounds in October, according to the Center for Real Estate Technology & Innovation (CRETI), which called it one of the strongest months of 2026.

Sources indicate that the money was heavily concentrated. Construction and development took roughly $872.4 million, or 52.8 percent of the total, while residential pulled in $604.4 million, or 36.6 percent. Three deals alone accounted for nearly 75 percent of October capital: Bedrock Robotics’ $600 million Series C, Unlock’s $433.1 million debt financing and ICON’s $200 million Series D.

It has been revealed that debt was a big part of the story. About $588.6 million, more than a third of the month’s total, came through debt rounds. That includes Unlock’s financing for its home-equity agreement platform and CrowdProperty’s roughly $133.5 million round for residential development lending.

That means much of October’s residential funding didn’t go into software at all but into financial products tied to home equity and property lending.

CRETI noted that funding signals investor conviction, not proof of ROI, and stated the bar for founders is rising to show a credible link between their technology and a material financial outcome.

The numbers suggest investors are betting less on latest real estate agent-facing software and more on the expensive, physical end of housing, such as building homes faster and cheaper and financing the transactions around them.

If that capital pays off, the bigger impact on agents and brokers may come indirectly, through more housing supply and new ways for homeowners to tap equity, rather than through the tools on their desks.

Airbnb plans to roll out its AI travel agent to consumers in the first half of 2027, the manufacturer remarked in its third-quarter shareholder letter, firming up a timeline it had previously pegged only as sometime in the next year.

Recent findings suggest that instead of a text-heavy chatbot, the AI agent will assemble a custom interface around each guest’s request, pulling from hundreds of travel-specific components such as maps, photos, comparisons, calendars and itineraries. It will also handle post-booking tasks like reservation changes, refunds, rebooking and payment issues, which Airbnb argues outside AI agents can’t easily do.

CEO Brian Chesky told analysts that general-purpose AI agents are fine for routine tasks but not for trip planning.

In a recent development, “Travel is aspirational,” Chesky mentioned. “Discovering where to go and where to stay is part of the experience.”.

In a recent development, the announcement came alongside a strong third quarter for Airbnb. Revenue grew 19 percent year over year to $4.87 billion, beating Wall Street estimates. Airbnb raised its 2026 growth forecast to the high teens, up from the mid-teens. Chesky called it the tech giant’s fastest revenue growth in more than three years.

Airbnb’s bet is one real estate portals and brokerages are weighing, too: that owning the search experience and the transaction behind it beats handing consumers off to general-purpose AI agents.

If a custom, visual AI agent wins over travelers, it’ll strengthen the case for real estate platforms to build their own AI home-search tools rather than relying on outside chatbots to send them buyers.

RealScout is now showing Zillow Preview listings from hundreds of participating brokerages in its collaborative home search platform, putting pre-MLS inventory in front of buyers searching with their own agents.

The integration, first announced in September, extends Zillow Preview’s reach beyond Zillow, Trulia and Realtor.com to RealScout’s network of more than 100,000 agents.

Sources indicate that preview listings appear in client searches and listing alerts that include Coming Soon properties. Buyers can message their agent directly about a home, and each Preview listing is replaced by its MLS listing once the home goes active. Agents and brokerages don’t need to opt in to see eligible listings.

RealScout CEO Andrew Flachner framed the move as a transparency play, with a not-so-subtle shot at private listing networks.

“Listing transparency comes down to whether a buyer can choose the agent they trust without worrying that the right home is hiding behind another brokerage’s velvet rope,” Flachner remarked in a statement. “With Zillow Preview listings from hundreds of brokerages now available in RealScout, agents can give their clients more of the market through the home search experience they already share.”.

Industry observers note that for agents, the integration means clients can see pre-MLS listings from participating brokerages in the search tool they already use, without signing up for Zillow or leaving the agent relationship. It also gives buyer’s agents an earlier look at upcoming inventory, which matters most in tight markets, where a few days’ head start can decide who gets a showing first.
