#41607. Breaking: Seller impersonation fraud is no longer a niche title problem

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (993 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Housingwire ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Seller impersonation fraud is no longer a niche title problem

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (993 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housingwire

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that two years is not a long time in housing.
  • In a recent development, in ALTA’s 2024 survey, 28% of title firms reported at least one seller impersonation fraud attempt in the prior calendar year.
  • In a recent development, seller impersonation fraud occurs when a criminal poses as the legitimate owner of a property and attempts to sell it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that two years is not a long time in housing. But in that short period, seller impersonation fraud has changed dramatically.

In a recent development, in ALTA’s 2024 survey, 28% of title firms reported at least one seller impersonation fraud attempt in the prior calendar year. In our latest study, that figure reached 59%. That’s more than double in two years, and that should concern everyone who depends on the integrity of a real estate transaction.

In a recent development, seller impersonation fraud occurs when a criminal poses as the legitimate owner of a property and attempts to sell it. At its core, this is an attack on property rights and on what is, for many Americans, their greatest source of wealth.

According to recent reports, for lenders, real estate professionals and others across housing, the stakes are equally clear. Every transaction depends on confidence that the person selling a property has the legal right to do so, that ownership is what the records say it is and that someone is looking closely enough to recognize when those things do not line up.

That is precisely the kind of problem the title industry was built to address.

Sources indicate that title professionals do far more than issue an insurance policy at the end of a transaction. Before closing, they examine ownership, investigate inconsistencies, resolve title defects, verify information and look for warning signs that could put a buyer, lender or property owner at risk. Seller impersonation fraud is a newer and increasingly sophisticated version of a challenge the industry has confronted for generations: determining whether a transaction is legitimate before property rights and money change hands.

And the threat is evolving quickly. Title professionals are encountering spoofed contact information, deepfake voice and image technology and increasingly sophisticated identity tactics. At the same time, criminals are broadening their targets beyond vacant land to vacation homes, rental properties, agricultural land and even primary residences, while also focusing on absentee owners, properties owned free and clear and properties tied to recently deceased owners.

The title industry is responding accordingly. 94% of firms report using multiple tools to detect fraud, with firms identifying an average of 5.3 tools as helpful, including identity verification systems, direct seller contact, multifactor authentication, approved notaries and knowledge-based authentication.

Sources indicate that but the most vital lesson is not that one particular tool works better than another. It is that effective fraud prevention is layered. It includes technology and verification, but it also depends on the judgment of experienced professionals who know when a piece of information does not fit with the rest of the transaction.

That prevention-first work is fundamental to title. Title insurance provides protection when covered problems arise, helping shield consumers from potentially devastating financial consequences. But the work starts long before a policy is issued. Title professionals work upfront to identify and resolve problems so that homebuyers, real estate professionals and lenders do not find themselves confronting a crisis after a transaction closes. In our latest survey, the clearance or curative process before closing was the most commonly reported stage for detecting seller impersonation fraud.

Much of that work is invisible when it succeeds. A suspicious transaction is questioned, an inconsistency is investigated, an identity is independently verified and a closing is stopped before money or property rights change hands. That is what prevention looks like.

It is also why conversations about housing affordability, efficiency and innovation should recognize the value of the protections already embedded in the transaction. Increasing efficiency and reducing costs are not merely worthy goals; they are important priorities for the entire housing industry. Title companies have invested heavily in technology and innovation to make transactions more efficient, and those investments are showing results: the inflation-adjusted cost of title insurance declined 32% between 2016 and 2024.

It has been revealed that we should continue that progress. But greater efficiency cannot mean removing safeguards designed to keep fraudulent transactions from closing, particularly at a moment when criminals themselves have more sophisticated tools at their fingertips.

The title industry will continue doing the work it was built to do. But protecting consumers from increasingly sophisticated fraud also creates opportunities for stronger partnerships across the housing ecosystem.

Lenders, real estate professionals and title professionals can reinforce consistent fraud-awareness messages and help consumers recognize warning signs before criminals gain their trust. Technology providers can continue developing tools that strengthen defenses. Law enforcement can investigate and prosecute the criminals behind these schemes.

Policymakers can support solutions that strengthen consumer protection while preserving the safeguards that help keep fraudulent transactions from closing. This is not about shifting responsibility from one part of the housing system to another. It is about recognizing that protecting consumers is most effective when everyone who touches a transaction understands the threat and reinforces the defenses already in place.

Seller impersonation fraud is the latest reminder that criminals will continue looking for new ways to exploit the housing market. The speed of its growth over just two years should serve as a warning.

Recent findings suggest that fortunately, our industry does not have to build a fraud-defense system from scratch. Title professionals already sit at a critical point in the transaction, examining ownership, resolving problems and helping prevent fraud before it becomes a loss.

The opportunity now is to build on that foundation together. By strengthening consumer education, sharing best practices and working closely with our housing partners and law enforcement, we can make it harder for criminals to exploit the transaction and help preserve something every participant in the housing market depends on: confidence that when a home changes hands, the transaction is legitimate and the property rights behind it are secure.

Chris Morton is CEO of the American Land Title Association (ALTA). This column does not necessarily reflect the opinion of HousingWire’s editorial department and its owners. To contact the editor responsible for this piece: [email protected].

On November 16, 2026, Lighter, the high-performance decentralized perpetuals exchange that settles on Ethereum with zero-knowledge proofs, activated Guardian mode and paused all withdrawals and new pool creation.

Industry observers note that on-chain data showed roughly $10.39M in USDC leaving the platform’s Ethereum settlement contract in a single withdrawal. Some researchers put the total impact closer to $15.5M across two large market-maker accounts. The attacker used a leaked API key tied to a trader’s account. The root cause was insecure custom signing code that reused cryptographic nonces, allowing the attacker to reconstruct the private key from public signatures.

With the key, the attacker created a public pool from the compromised account, acquired most of its shares, moved the victim’s USDC into the pool, and redeemed it. Importantly, Lighter’s core protocol and smart contracts were never compromised; this was an account-level key compromise, not a smart-contract exploit. Funds were rapidly swapped into ETH, with portions routed to Hyperliquid. LIT initially dropped by 20% on the news before buyers stepped in.

Lighter moved fast. Within hours, the team publicly confirmed the cause, named the attacker wallet, and made clear that the protocol itself remained intact. The Security Council recovered approximately $5M in USDC and returned it to the affected trader. Guardian mode was deactivated the same day and withdrawals resumed. Fresh safeguards followed immediately: wallet signatures are now required for transfers into public pools, API key signatures are non-public, IP allowlists are planned, per-key permission limits are in place, and automated monitoring for nonce reuse is active.

Sources indicate that owners running custom or third-party signing software were strongly advised to rotate keys and switch to Lighter’s official SDKs. The message was clear: the platform treated the incident as a user-key hygiene concern and hardened the surrounding controls without ever having a core vulnerability.

That combination of transparent communication, partial recovery, rapid resumption of operations, and concrete security upgrades is exactly the kind of response that historically flips sentiment from fear to “they handled it cleanly.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the Census Bureau reported a surge in multifamily construction starts in October. Apartment industry analysts don’t buy it.

Industry data show a shrinking apartment construction pipeline. Developers say they’re breaking ground on fewer projects and expect to start even fewer in 2027.

Starts in buildings with five or more units rose 25.5% from September to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 433,000, the Census Bureau and the Department of Housing and Urban Development reported Wednesday. That was 22% above the year-earlier rate. Permits fell 5.2% to an annual rate of 475,000, reversing a September increase and leaving authorizations 0.4% below their year-earlier level.

“The vibes among multifamily builders today are as bearish as I’ve seen since about 2010,” apartment market analyst Jay Parsons wrote on LinkedIn. He pointed to the Federal Reserve’s September rate hike and signals of further increases. Higher rates make projects harder to finance, he noted, by raising borrowing costs while putting downward pressure on property values.

Recent findings suggest that parsons said the federal figures don’t square with what developers are telling him or with private-sector data. He rejects the idea that the discrepancy could be chalked up to monthly volatility and questions whether the Census Bureau’s survey of permit holders reliably captures multifamily starts.

Sources indicate that “The pullback in construction activity is broad-based,” Cushman & Wakefield noted in its third-quarter U.S. multifamily report. Construction pipelines shrank from a year earlier in more than 70% of the 90 markets the firm tracks.

Sources indicate that the steepest declines came in markets that built most aggressively during the boom. In Sarasota, Florida, units under construction as a share of existing apartment inventory fell by 7.9 percentage points. Savannah, Georgia, and Austin, Texas, also posted sharp declines.

Recent findings suggest that pipelines expanded in just 25 markets. Cushman & Wakefield singled out Palm Beach and the Bay Area, where it noted stronger rent growth had improved the economics of latest development.

Recent findings suggest that another relevant data indicator, the AIA/Deltek Architecture Billings Index® (ABI) score remained well below 50 at 44.9 for the month, as billings have not been in consistently positive territory for more than four years now. This index is a leading indicator primarily for latest Commercial Real Estate (CRE) investment, including multi-family residential. According to Calculated Risk, a housing blog hosted by analyst Bill McBride, “multi-family billings have been below 50 for 49 of the last 51 months.”.

Meanwhile, apartment demand through September ran at its strongest pace since 2021, and the national vacancy rate fell to a three-year low of 8.6% in the third quarter. Net absorption totaled nearly 350,000 units, up 14% from the same period last year, while deliveries fell 25% to just over 250,000 units. Asking rents rose 2.3% from a year earlier to $1,950, the fastest pace of growth since early 2023.

“A resilient economy continues to support household formation and renter demand, while higher interest rates and elevated home prices have widened the affordability gap between renting and owning,” Cushman & Wakefield stated.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • On-chain data shows the attacker behind the $6.3 billion Binance theft depositing about $4 million into three Binance deposit addresses.
  • Industry observers note that at the same time, Binance's first post-hack reserve snapshot reveals its biggest assets covered with buffers as small as 2.7 ETH and $6 of USDT.
  • Some of the money stolen from Binance has started going back to Binance.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

On-chain data shows the attacker behind the $6.3 billion Binance theft depositing about $4 million into three Binance deposit addresses.

Industry observers note that at the same time, Binance's first post-hack reserve snapshot reveals its biggest assets covered with buffers as small as 2.7 ETH and $6 of USDT. Binance's full zero-knowledge proof of those figures is due by Tuesday.

Some of the money stolen from Binance has started going back to Binance.

Blockchain intelligence firm Arkham has flagged the entity it tracks as "Binance Hacker" depositing about $4 million into three Binance deposit addresses. Arkham states those addresses "likely represent nested service(s)." These are third-party exchanges that use Binance for liquidity and custody, giving their own customers deposit addresses that sit on Binance's infrastructure.

If Arkham is right, the hacker isn't depositing into an ordinary Binance account. The money would be going to smaller platforms that operate through Binance. Exchanges have long known this is a weak point for stolen funds moving into normal trading. Either way, Binance is now receiving stolen funds at its own deposit addresses while it works to show customers it has replaced what was taken.

The FBI has attributed the October 29 theft to North Korea. The deposits come at a sensitive moment. Binance has just published its first reserve snapshot since the hack and has promised a full cryptographic proof of it by Tuesday.

$4 million is a small slice of a theft worth about $6.3 billion, but it matters for two reasons.

Industry observers note that it shows how the laundering works. Nested services are a common way into the regulated financial system. A third-party platform that relies on Binance for custody may run weaker identity checks on its own consumers. Funds deposited there can be swapped and withdrawn without the hacker ever opening a Binance account.

Binance can act on it. Binance can't freeze bitcoin and ether sitting in wallets nobody controls, and it doesn't control the stablecoins that issuers like Tether and Circle have frozen. Deposits that land at its own addresses are different: they are on Binance's platform, so Binance can freeze them itself. One of the first tests of how Binance handles the money still in the hacker's hands is whether it freezes these funds and identifies the services that own the addresses.

While the hacker's funds move, Binance has been rebuilding its reserves. Its proof-of-reserves page now shows:.

The first page covers Binance's six largest assets. Customer balances are what consumers hold. Reserves are on-chain wallet balances, including assets held with outside custodians.

The second page has four more assets, and two of them stand out:.

It has been revealed that why USD1 and RLUSD matter: these are two of the stablecoins whose issuers froze stolen funds after the attack. World Liberty Financial froze $27 million of USD1, and Ripple began freezing RLUSD the same night. Both now show reserves above what Binance owes customers.

Assets with outside custodians: part of several reserves sits with outside custodians rather than in Binance's own exchange wallets:.

Asset | Held with third-party custodians.

According to recent reports, the striking part isn't that the ratios reach 100%. It's how closely they stop there.

In a recent development, compared with October's report: Binance's previous monthly report, published in early October before the hack, revealed BTC at 100.35% and USDT at 103.88%. ETH was already at exactly 100.00%. After the theft:.

It has been revealed that not every asset is that tight. USDC, ZEC and BNB carry buffers of 1.3% to 6%. The thinnest buffers are in BTC, ETH, USDT and SOL, which are among the assets the attacker took in the largest amounts.

How Binance claims it got here: the pattern fits Binance's account of replacing the stolen assets in stages. It reported 80% replaced on Friday, 90% on Saturday and 95% on Sunday. The remaining 5% is in less-liquid tokens it is still buying. The money came from:.

Binance confirmed taking 7,499 BTC from SAFU and has pledged to refill the fund to about $1 billion.

In a recent development, what the snapshot can't show: it was taken a little over a day after the theft, once the rebuild was under way. It indicates the balance sheet after the replacement, not how large the gap was on October 29.

Binance indicates the full proof takes 40 to 50 hours to compute. Its latest upgrade says it will be ready "by Tuesday, 2026-11-03 (UTC)." The system is open source, in Binance's zkmerkle-proof-of-solvency repository.

What the proof guarantees, according to the project's circuit design document:.

The design also guards against a "dummy user attack" identified by Ethereum Foundation researcher Enrico Bottazzi. In that attack, fake accounts holding cheap tokens are used to offset debts in major assets.

What it doesn't prove: the reserve side. The project's verifier config describes the totals as information "published by CEX, it represents CEX's liability." The reserve figures are checked a different way, against the wallet addresses Binance publishes through the page's "Download All Address" option.

According to recent reports, what customers can do: each user can get a Merkle proof for their account and check it against the published root. They can use the verifier code in Binance's repository rather than Binance's own interface. That doesn't prove Binance is solvent, but it confirms the user's balance was counted.

Binance has rebuilt its reserves to 100% across its ten largest assets, but on several of them the buffer is only a few coins. Meanwhile, stolen funds are reaching its deposit addresses through platforms that run on its infrastructure. Tuesday's proof can confirm customer balances. It can't show how Binance handles the stolen money arriving at its own door.

Payhawk Ltd., a startup that helps enterprises manage their business expenses, has raised $280 million in funding.

The Series C round was led by Goldman Sachs’ growth equity arm. The bank was joined by Greenoaks, Lightspeed and more than a half-dozen others. Payhawk stated today that it’s now valued at $2 billion.

In a recent development, issuing corporate credit cards to employees historically involved a weeks-long wait. Payhawk operates a platform that enables companies to create virtual cards in a few seconds and concern physical ones in five days. According to the organization, customers can configure a card to expire automatically at the end of the project for which it’s needed.

In a recent development, accounting teams can set spending limits to avoid cost overruns. Payhawk makes it possible to tie purchase caps to a business project, a specific merchant or a broad product category.

Sources indicate that companies can optionally connect their cards to Payhawk-operated business accounts. They support payments in more than 115 currencies. According to the software maker, its accounts’ currency exchange rates are up to 90% lower than those charged by traditional banks.

It has been revealed that syncing corporate card spending to a tech giant’s accounting ledger is a multistep process. First, workers must scan the receipt issued in connection with a purchase and send it to the finance team. From there, an accountant categorizes the purchase and verifies it through a process known as reconciliation.

In a recent development, payhawk automates the workflow using an artificial intelligence agent. Additionally, it flags cost-cutting opportunities such as unnecessary software-as-a-service subscriptions.

Sources indicate that A second AI agent speeds up procurement initiatives. It’s accessible through a chat interface that enables workers to request items in natural language. If a request is missing certain details, the agent can point out what additional information is needed. From there, it automatically seeks approvals from relevant executives.

Payhawk also automates a number of other tasks. It includes a tool that reduces the amount of work involved in changing business trip looks. Additionally, the company has built an AI engine that enables new users to customize its platform by uploading documents such as spending policies.

“Through our technology, finance departments can benefit from ‘zero-touch finance,’ where neither the finance professional nor the employee deals with any admin work,” remarked Payhawk co-founder and Chief Executive Officer Hristo Borisov. “Seventy-seven percent of our customers use our agents daily across financial control, procurement, travel and reporting to save time and money for their businesses.”.

According to recent reports, payhawk notes it still has 70% of its previous funding round, a $100 million investment that closed in 2022. The tech giant will use the proceeds from today’s Series C raise to enhance its AI capabilities.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Blue Owl is lining up a $513 million offering of commercial mortgage-backed bonds to help pay for a Virginia data center it bought that Amazon $AMZN leases, according to Bloomberg.

It has been revealed that blue Owl Digital Infrastructure Trust, through a subsidiary, completed the acquisition of the 54-megawatt facility in Gainesville, Virginia, on Nov. 10 for $779.5 million, the company remarked in an SEC filing. The filing said the property is 100% leased to a hyperscaler customer and that the trust paid with its available cash and a new property-level mortgage loan.

In a recent development, citigroup $C is running the bond sale, according to Bloomberg. The deal includes a $375 million portion of bonds, averaging five years in life, which Fitch Ratings and Kroll Bond Rating Agency are expected to grade AAA. Initial pricing guidance for that tranche is a spread of 1.95 percentage points above the benchmark.

A $112 million tranche that likewise has a five-year average life is expected to receive an AA rating from Kroll, with guidance of a 2.6-percentage-point spread to the benchmark, according to Bloomberg. A $26 million slice that Kroll is expected to rate AA- is being sold in a private placement.

The securities are secured by a mortgage covering the property, known as Project Crossing III, according to Bloomberg. Amazon's lease started in March, extends to 2041, and gives the tenant a pair of five-year renewal options. Amazon had no role in putting the financing together. Representatives for Blue Owl and Citigroup declined to comment, Bloomberg stated.

Sources indicate that in the filing, Blue Owl noted the property owner entered a loan agreement on Nov. 10 with Citibank and Wells Fargo $WFC for a $512.6 million floating-rate mortgage loan. The loan matures in December 2028, with one 12-month extension option. It carries interest at one-month Term SOFR plus 2 percentage points through Nov. 9, 2027, rising to 2.25 percentage points after that through the initial maturity date.

Blue Owl Digital Infrastructure Operating Partnership provided a non-recourse guaranty for the loan, the filing said.

Industry observers note that the property ranks as the third facility built within the Gainesville Crossing Data Center campus, according to Bloomberg. The campus is projected to grow to five buildings with a combined capacity of 326 megawatts.

Japanese-owned builders are cutting U.S. outlooks: what’s next?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that following our article last month on the likelihood of decreased investment in the U.S.
  • Sources indicate that it goes without saying that the operating environment has been tough for homebuilders, whether they’re based in the U.S.
  • With expectations lower, we expect shifts within U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that following our article last month on the likelihood of decreased investment in the U.S. by Japanese builders, we’re now looking at what recent results and forecasts from the Japanese-owned homebuilders may mean for decisions about the operations and structures of their U.S. operations.

Sources indicate that it goes without saying that the operating environment has been tough for homebuilders, whether they’re based in the U.S. or elsewhere. As a result, the three Japanese homebuilders with significant U.S. operations – Sekisui House, Sumitomo Forestry, and Daiwa House – have all lowered their U.S. forecasts.

With expectations lower, we expect shifts within U.S. subsidiaries as they work to cut expenses and maximize profitability. This expectation was reinforced by Sumitomo Forestry’s recent comment that “realizing synergies between Tri Pointe Homes and our other U.S. housing companies is the most important issue for recovering earnings next fiscal year.”.

In recent weeks, Daiwa House and Sumitomo Forestry have lowered their forecasts for their U.S. operations. Daiwa House now expects about $4.88 billion in revenue from its U.S. homebuilding operations in fiscal 2026 (ending in March 2027), down slightly from its prior forecast of $5.08 billion. However, the revised forecast includes 1,000 more closings than the prior forecast, with 9,000 closings now expected in fiscal 2026 versus 8,000 in the prior forecast.

Given the challenging environment as of late, this increase is not due to stronger activity, but to the inclusion of closings for recent acquisitions.

Sources indicate that we believe the higher closings outlook likely reflects the incorporation of forecasts for Stanley Martin’s recent acquisitions of United Homes (acquired in May 2026) and Holiday Builders (acquired in July 2026). We believe these two acquisitions will add roughly 1,300 closings in fiscal 2026 and approximately $450 million in revenue, more than offsetting a shortfall in closings from U.S. operations excluding these acquisitions.

We estimate that, excluding the acquisitions, Daiwa House expects approximately $650 million less in revenue for the year than it had anticipated in August 2026, with much of that impact coming in the second half of the fiscal year (as the August forecast was released in the middle of its fiscal second quarter, when there would have been reasonable certainty about the forecast for the first half of the year).

Recent findings suggest that sumitomo Forestry now expects $7.01 billion in revenue from its U.S. home sales in 2026, a $776 million reduction from its prior forecast of $7.79 billion in August 2026. This reflects a 1,455-home reduction in its closings forecast relative to the prior forecast, with much of the reduction coming from lower expectations for the fourth quarter, since Sumitomo Forestry issued its August forecast halfway through its third quarter. Sumitomo Forestry now expects 12,705 closings in 2026, down from its prior expectation of 14,160 closings. These expectations include the contribution from Sumitomo Forestry’s May 2026 acquisition of Tri Pointe Homes.

Sekisui House will release fiscal Q3 results in several weeks, given its January 31st fiscal year-end.

Recent findings suggest that while Sekisui House has implemented an initiative to unify its U.S. operations under the Sekisui House USA entity, Daiwa House and Sumitomo Forestry have generally taken a hands-off, decentralized approach, allowing their U.S. subsidiaries to run their operations. However, we would not be surprised to see a shift toward greater focus on finding synergies in the U.S. operations given the lower expected profitability levels in 2026 (and likely 2027).

In a recent development, the relatively low margin levels reported by Daiwa House (expecting a 6.4% operating margin from its U.S. homebuilding operations in fiscal 2026) and Sumitomo Forestry (expecting a 6.7% recurring income margin in 2026) come amid an increased focus on capital efficiency, often described by Japanese companies as “improving capital profitability.” While we think some of the effort to improve capital efficiency will come from reducing capital employed to control land, we also expect a heightened focus on profitability, given that internal expectations likely point to a further decline in profit margins in 2027.

Sumitomo Forestry’s statements accompanying its Q3 results were consistent with its focus on profitability and on seeking synergies: “Our U.S. housing companies, including Tri Pointe Homes, are at the moment reviewing their staffing structures to reduce costs. In addition, we believe that realizing synergies between Tri Pointe Homes and our other U.S. housing companies is the most important issue for recovering earnings next fiscal year.”.

We’re curious to see Sumitomo Forestry’s approach to achieving synergies and whether those synergies will be limited to areas such as accounting and purchasing, or whether there will be a broader effort elsewhere.

If the aim is more integrated operations, it will be interesting given the make-up of its U.S. subsidiaries, with DRB generating 6,960 closings in 2025, Tri Pointe with 4,947 closings, and the four remaining builders (Bloomfield Homes, Edge Homes, MainVue Homes, and Southern Impression Homes) closing 3,302 homes in aggregate in 2025.

According to recent reports, having two entities – DRB and Tri Pointe – with such large shares of total activity likely means that one of them would end up with some form of control or oversight of the U.S. operations. Sumitomo Forestry potentially hinted at the need for cost savings at Tri Pointe, noting that Tri Pointe’s profit margin was lower than that of the other five existing builders and citing “its high expense ratio associated with its nationwide operations” and the impact of price competition in California.

Recent findings suggest that daiwa House has remarked less about its efforts to achieve synergies among its U.S. subsidiaries, but we would expect this to be a priority. However, for Daiwa House, decisions about control and oversight are likely more straightforward given the scale difference, as Stanley Martin (approximately 7,500 closings in 2025 on a pro forma basis, including United Homes and Holiday Builders) accounts for approximately 75% of Daiwa House USA’s total closings based on reported 2025 closings.

We expect to hear more about synergy looks over the next several months, given builders’ cautious approach to 2027 amid ongoing weakness. Sumitomo Forestry noted that it has “not seen a recovery in market conditions or in orders for October,” and added, “at this point, we believe it is highly likely that challenging conditions will continue, including during next year’s spring sales season.”.

According to recent reports, we would not confuse these synergy efforts with retrenchment, and we believe they reflect a refinement of their U.S. operations as these companies digest and integrate their recent acquisitions.

Daiwa House, Sekisui House, and Sumitomo Forestry all have meaningful scale. Each has at least 10,000 annual closings on a pro forma basis, based on reported 2025 closings. This refinement period during the downturn occurs as the parent companies work to improve corporate-level leverage ratios, shifting the emphasis from external expansion to operational improvement.

Assuming these synergies and operational improvements are not disruptive to the business, we expect these three companies to emerge from the difficult conditions with a stronger operating platform and to be well positioned for further growth.

CVD shows the difference between the volume of market buy orders and market sell orders, and a negative CVD means that sellers were more active on the exchange.

Over the same period, the CVD on the spot markets of OKX, Bybit and Binance stood at $240.3 million, $65.17 million and $51.88 million, respectively, so buyers were more active on these three exchanges.

The price of Bitcoin went down from $81,188 on Nov. 4 to $61,956 on Nov. 14, according to CoinGlass data, and the decline amounted to around 24%. On Sunday, Bitcoin recovered to around $65,400.

The data comes amid claims that Binance has been pushing the price of Bitcoin down. The exchange lost $6.4 billion in a hack on Oct. 29, and some owners on X then claimed that Binance was selling crypto to cover its losses. Two weeks after the attack, Binance published a Proof of Reserves report that demonstrated client balances on the exchange were fully backed.

This week, Binance founder Changpeng Zhao shared a comparison of Bitcoin charts ahead of the SpaceX and Anthropic IPOs and called it "an interesting analysis." Several consumers in the replies to his post blamed the drop in Bitcoin on selling by Binance.

Binance is the largest crypto exchange by trading volume, and a large share of futures liquidations takes place on the platform. On Nov. 13, crypto exchanges liquidated 187,389 traders for a total of $1.65 billion in 24 hours, and 88% of that amount came from long positions, according to CoinGlass. Still, the CVD on the Binance spot market has stayed positive since Oct. 31.

Industry observers note that coinbase is the custodian for most U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs, including BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust, and many U.S. institutional investors trade on the platform through Coinbase Prime.

Recent findings suggest that anthropic is set to start trading on Nasdaq on Nov. 19, and the selling on Coinbase comes ahead of the listing. Fundstrat managing partner Tom Lee has called the recent drawdown in Bitcoin a temporary rotation of money into mega-IPOs, and in the 50 days before the Anthropic IPO, Bitcoin has lost around 18%.

Sources indicate that the CVD on Coinbase fell most sharply between Nov. 10 and Nov. 14, and Bitcoin dropped below $70,000 during this period, according to CoinGlass data.

According to recent reports, XRP price saw a sell-off over the weekend, with liquidations accelerating in the last 24 hours. At the time of writing, XRP was down 3.43% in the last 24 hours to $0.969 and down 17% weekly.

Industry observers note that onchain data platform CoinGlass seeks to answer why XRP's price is down. Its analysis, generated from the past 24 hours of futures, spot and ETF data, points to three indicators that help explain the pressure on XRP.

First is a 'long squeeze,' which increased selling pressure on the price. Long traders have taken the biggest hit during the latest decline. CoinGlass data shows that XRP long liquidations reached $43.17 million over the past 24 hours, accounting for about 91% of total liquidations.

Second, open interest has fallen as traders, largely longs, close positions. XRP open interest has fallen 5.53% in the past 24 hours to $2.03 billion.

Sources indicate that thirdly, XRP is presently in negative funding at -0.0082%. Negative funding in perpetual futures markets means that short sellers are paying long sellers to keep positions open, a sign traders are bearish on the market.

XRP fell for 10 straight days from November 5 to November 14, 2026. Price lost momentum after losing the daily MA 200 at the close of October. The cryptocurrency lost another crucial support in early October, the daily MA 50, weakening bulls.

Stablecoin supply is shrinking fast, dropping $17 billion over the last month, the steepest drop since 2022. As holders swap stablecoins to fiat, they drain buying power from BTC and crypto, analysts at Glassnode mentioned.

It will be watched if buying power returns to the market; according to Bitwise CEO Matt Hougan, "There will be a massive buying opportunity at some point, but it's hard to say when.".

Sources indicate that the daily RSI has entered oversold levels, with the possibility of a relief rally in the coming session. Such a recovery, if sustained, will target the daily MA 50 and 200 at $1.25 and $1.30. Further downside is expected to find support at $0.77.

In a recent development, BOSTON, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- PTC (NASDAQ: PTC) today confirmed an expansion of its FedRAMP offerings for U.S. federal agencies and contractors. PTC's Windchill+Â® product lifecycle management (PLM) solution is now available on Microsoft Azure Government within PTC Cloud Services, and PTC is introducing its OnshapeÂ® Government Federal solution, a FedRAMP Moderate Equivalent environment for engineering teams working with Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI). The two newly introduced offerings also support compliance with the Department of Defense's Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) program for protecting CUI.

Sources indicate that windchill+ is the only direct, full-stack SaaS PLM solution certified on the FedRAMP Marketplace. PTC Cloud Services is certified at the FedRAMP Class C (Moderate) baseline (NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5), so agencies can rely on an existing certification rather than running their own security review.

Sources indicate that onshape Government Federal is the only cloud-native CAD and PDM with a FedRAMP Moderate Equivalent attestation based on NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5. Built on AWS GovCloud (US), it expands its existing support for ITAR and EAR workloads. It also integrates with the ArenaÂ® PLM for AWS GovCloud solution, giving organizations a connected CAD, PDM, and PLM environment across engineering, quality, and supply chain workflows.

"Aerospace and defense organizations build and maintain some of the most complex, mission-critical products in the world," stated Jon Stevenson, Chief Product Officer, PTC. "For nearly a decade, we've invested in cloud solutions that meet federal security requirements, and we aim to continue that investment so these customers can count on PTC from product design through service.".

PTC Cloud Services first achieved FedRAMP authorization in 2017, and PTC has expanded its federal portfolio steadily ever since. In addition to Windchill+ and Onshape, federal agencies and contractors can choose from these PTC solutions to manage product data while meeting federal security requirements:.

It has been revealed that across its portfolio, PTC is delivering on its vision for the Intelligent Product Lifecycle: enabling manufacturers to build a modern product data foundation, extend that data across the enterprise, and unlock AI-powered transformation. Broader use of product data enables companies to bring higher-quality products to market faster, manage complexity at scale, and support new digital business models.

About PTCPTC (NASDAQ: PTC) is a global software company that enables manufacturers and product companies to digitally transform how they design, manufacture, and service the physical products that the world relies on. Headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, PTC employs over 7,000 people and supports more than 30,000 customers globally.

Breaking: Everpure beats expectations as AI accelerates revenue growth for ninth straight quarter

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1235 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Siliconangle

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Data center infrastructure tech giant Everpure Inc.
  • According to recent reports, the storage and data management hardware firm reported earnings before certain costs such as stock compensation of 86 cents per share, easily beating Wall Street’s consensus estimate of 77 cents.
  • Chairman and Chief Executive Charles Giancarlo (pictured) noted the results reinforce the tech giant’s status as a trusted partner for enterprises.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 21:10 EST / NOVEMBER 18 2026.

Data center infrastructure tech giant Everpure Inc. posted third-quarter earnings and revenue that surpassed analysts’ expectations and raised its full-year forecast for the third successive quarter, and its stock gained just over 4% in after-hours trading today.

According to recent reports, the storage and data management hardware firm reported earnings before certain costs such as stock compensation of 86 cents per share, easily beating Wall Street’s consensus estimate of 77 cents. Revenue for the period rose 51% from a year earlier to $1.5 billion, surpassing the analyst’s target of $1.33 billion by a comfortable margin.

Chairman and Chief Executive Charles Giancarlo (pictured) noted the results reinforce the tech giant’s status as a trusted partner for enterprises. “As organizations work to break down data silos and modernize their data estates, our growth across both core and new, high-growth markets indicates we are uniquely equipped to solve their most complex data challenges at scale,” he added.

Recent findings suggest that everpure, formerly known as Pure Storage, is a pioneer of all-flash data storage hardware and unified data management software for applications, cloud environments, analytics workloads and, increasingly, artificial intelligence workloads. Specifically for AI, it provides enterprises and cloud infrastructure providers with the high-speed, cost- and power-efficient data storage and management solutions they need to keep pace with the high-end accelerators that process model training and inference workloads.

In a recent development, the company rebranded in February 2026 as part of an effort to emphasize its vision of “data primacy,” which positions its products as the central data intelligence and governance layer for AI. By integrating closely with Nvidia Corp.’s graphics processing units and using tools such as its Data Intelligence software and its FlashBlade servers, it claims to be able to prepare data, speed up inference and lower GPU and storage costs.

In a recent development, AI has helped Everpure to accelerate its momentum this year, and it beat the Street’s targets across all major metrics in the last quarter. Adjusted operating income reached $345 million, an impressive $70 million above its prior guidance. Product revenue, derived from the sale of storage systems, came to $948 million, up 77% from a year earlier, while subscription services revenue was up 20%. Net income for the quarter came to $100.4 million, up from $54.8 million in the same period one year ago.

The tech giant said its remaining performance obligations, which refers to the value of contracts already signed but not yet realized as revenue, ended the quarter at $4.2 billion, up 44%.

According to recent reports, NAND Research analyst Steve McDowell told SiliconANGLE that a primary reason for Everpure’s growth is the rising cost of memory and flash storage, which has allowed the tech giant to bump up the prices of its storage products quite substantially this year without any negative impact on demand. “But it’s notable that Everpure continues to outperform the broader storage market, and the numbers it’s putting up suggests it’s taking market share away from its rivals,” he remarked.

Everpure’s growth has been accelerating for more than two years now. In August, the tech giant noted its revenue had grown for eight successive quarters, and today’s report makes that nine. Over the last five quarters, it has grown by 16%, 20%, 35%, 38% and 51%. “It’s the third consecutive quarter of growth above 35%,” McDowell said. “At the same time, it has been growing its product margins even in the face of those rising component costs and supply chain challenges. Everpure’s team is demonstrating strong execution to do this.”.

Giancarlo noted on a conference call that much of that momentum has to do with AI. During the quarter, it won a design contract with one of the top five largest hyperscale cloud companies, he added.

In a recent development, according to McDowell, the only real blot on Everpure’s results was the slight drop in its subscription margins, but even this was more than offset by its increased product margins. “This was not addressed on the conference call, and it’s something I’ll be watching going forward.”.

According to recent reports, however, there are serious questions regarding whether Everpure’s growth momentum has peaked. For the current quarter, it’s forecasting sales of between $1.5 billion and $1.52 billion, which would amount to growth of between 42% and 43%.

Industry observers note that the forecast is still ahead of the Street’s target of $1.49 billion in sales, but in order to keep accelerating its growth, it would need to generate fourth-quarter revenue of at least $1.6 billion, which is about $83 million higher than the top end of its forecast range. That’s not impossible, because Everpure actually beat the top end of its range by $125 million in the quarter just gone.

Recent findings suggest that mcDowell said one reason to be optimistic that Everpure can keep accelerating is that it has spent the last year expanding its offerings, without showing any material impact on its bottom line from those efforts. “Its hyperscale business is only just starting to impact revenue, so most of this growth has been from its traditional products,” the analyst said. “That tells me there’s still significant upside to come.”.

Even if Everpure’s momentum slows, it’s still on track to deliver an impressive financial year. The firm also raised its full-year revenue guidance from a prior range of $5.03 billion to $5.07 billion to a fresh range of $5.2 billion to $5.21 billion. Wall Street analysts are modeling full-year sales of $5.06 billion.

In a recent development, blockstream CEO Adam Back has commented on the rebound of Bitcoin after its overnight drop to a four-month low. On Sunday, Back posted a Bitfinex chart of Bitcoin on X with a one-word caption: "Bouncy.".

Back created Hashcash, the proof-of-work scheme that Satoshi Nakamoto cited in the original Bitcoin whitepaper, and he was one of the first people Satoshi contacted about Bitcoin.

In a recent development, early Sunday, the price of Bitcoin fell to $62,029 on Bitfinex, a level it had not seen since July. After that, Bitcoin went up by 5.5%, and the chart shared by Back demonstrates the price at $65,487.

Recent findings suggest that bouncy. 🟩+5.5% overnight👍 https://t.co/fzspLHXcbr.

Bitcoin has lost around 20% over the past month, according to price data by TradingView. Its all-time high of $126,000 was set in October 2025, and Bitcoin is now trading at about half of that level.

Earlier this month, Bitcoin fell below its 200-day moving average near $73,000. On Nov. 13, crypto exchanges liquidated $1.65 billion in 24 hours, and most of the liquidated positions were longs, according to CoinGlass. Besides, investors withdrew almost $3 billion from U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs over the past few weeks, according to SoSoValue.

The decline comes after Binance lost $6.4 billion in a hack in October. Fundstrat managing partner Tom Lee has also called the recent drawdown a rotation of money into mega-IPOs, and Anthropic is set to start trading on Nasdaq on Nov. 19.

It has been revealed that on Nov. 12, Back told CNBC that he still expects Bitcoin to reach $1 million in the current cycle. "Personally I have a bet on Bitcoin to top a million by the end of the cycle, which is later in 2028," Back remarked.

Sources indicate that according to Back, around 95% of the capital managed by large asset managers, mutual funds and model portfolios has not yet entered Bitcoin. "We're still 95% or more of that to come in the following years," he said.

It has been revealed that back calls Bitcoin "better gold" because of its capped supply and simple verification. He expects banks and pension funds to become the third wave of demand for Bitcoin, and Vanguard has already allowed its clients to trade crypto ETFs.

"I think we're in the early innings of a bull market cycle," Back added.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

New Research of 10,000 Consumers Finds McDonald's Owns the Cheap Meal but No Brand Owns Dinner, While Starbucks and Dunkin' Hold 48% of U.S. Coffee Share of Mind.

Sources indicate that BOSTON, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Zappi, the leading consumer insights platform helping global brands win with consumers, today released Who Owns the QSR and Coffee Market?, a study of 10,000 U.S. and U.K. consumers that maps which fast food and coffee brands people think of, and for which moments. The headline for fast food: the value war is buying visits, not hearts. McDonald's dominates the cheap meal, while dinner, family meals and treat moments have no clear owner. In coffee, Starbucks and Dunkin' hold 48% of U.S. Mental Market Share, and drive-thru challengers like 7 Brew and Dutch Bros are winning younger consumers by owning the drink itself.

Recent findings suggest that as fast food chains compete hard on price, the research reveals what discounting does and doesn't win. McDonald's takes 17% of all associations for "a meal that doesn't cost much," more than four points above its overall share and the strongest claim on value in every U.S. region except the West, where Taco Bell leads. Yet no brand gets more than about 10% of associations for dinner, feeding the family, treating yourself, comfort after a tough day or eating with friends. Chick-fil-A leads "treat myself" with just 9%, and chicken chains as a group over-index on that moment by seven points.

In a recent development, "Fast food's value war is focused on securing repeat visits, not hearts," said Nataly Kelly, Chief Marketing Officer at Zappi. "Price wins you the busy Tuesday lunch. It doesn't make you the place people want for Friday dinner or after a bad day, and right now no chain owns those moments. That's the most valuable open space in fast food, and the chicken brands are already over-indexing there while the burger giants are fixated on price.".

Coffee is a two-brand market by comparison, with each giant selling something different. Starbucks leads with 28% of U.S. coffee Mental Market Share and owns the sit-down moments, from somewhere to work or study to meeting up with someone. Dunkin', at 20%, owns speed and food: coffee on the go, starting the day and a sweet treat. Drive-thru challengers own the drink itself (cold and refreshing, a pick-me-up, a weekend day out), and that's where younger consumers lean. Geography reshapes the race as well. Dunkin' edges Starbucks 27% to 26% in the Northeast, Dutch Bros holds 13% in the West, two points behind Dunkin', and 7 Brew ranks third in the South at 9%.

"Starbucks sells a place and Dunkin' sells speed. The drive-thru brands figured out they could sell the drink, and younger customers are buying it," mentioned Kelly. "7 Brew doesn't need to beat Starbucks nationally. Third place in the South already makes it the brand Dunkin' has to watch there, and the drive-thru window is where coffee's next fight will be decided.".

Additional key findings from the report include:.

Zappi surveyed 10,000 recent fast food and coffee shop customers between October 29 and November 1, 2026, across five markets: the U.S. Northeast, Midwest, South and West, and the U.K. Each market had separate fast food and coffee surveys of 1,000 respondents, together covering 102 brands and 15 everyday moments such as "breakfast on the go.".

Results are weighted to reflect each market's population, and U.S. national figures combine the four regions weighted by population. "Younger" refers to consumers aged 18 to 45 (Gen Z and Millennials). Mental Market Share is a brand's share of all the associations consumers make between the brands in its category and those everyday moments; fast food and coffee are measured separately, so their scores aren't directly comparable.

To explore the full findings, regional rankings and emerging brands to watch, download Zappi's Who Owns the QSR and Coffee Market.

Xsolla ZK, Inc. is introducing Xsolla Gas (XLA), the native token of Xsolla ZK — a blockchain network built for games. XLA is designed to pay the network fees that arise when players transfer or share eligible digital items on Xsolla ZK.

For players who’d rather not download and set up a separate wallet, Xsolla Gas Station, offered by Xsolla (USA), Inc., can cover those fees. There, players buy XLA-NT, a non-transferable gas credit used only to pay network fees on Xsolla ZK. (Xsolla Gas Station sells only XLA-NT.).

Players want more from the games and brands they follow, and developers want new ways to engage them. Digital items have evolved well beyond cosmetics — players now collect them from their favorite games. But letting players keep, share, and give away those items has long been complicated.

Recent findings suggest that most digital items today live on a single game’s backend. Players generally can’t transfer them to friends or carry them into another game, and the items simply vanish if a game shuts down. Blockchain-backed items stay with the players who collect them — but transferring them requires a network fee, which traditionally means setting up and managing a separate digital wallet and acquiring the right token to pay. That friction adds up.

Xsolla ZK is designed to remove that friction. Xsolla’s existing payment, monetization, and distribution products can now support blockchain-backed items — giving developers a latest way to monetize and distribute digital items, and giving players new ways to keep them and pass them on.

Players use Xsolla Gas to cover the network fees required to transfer or share a digital item held in their Xsolla Backpack.

Recent findings suggest that xsolla Backpack is an inventory for the digital items a player owns. Items issued to the Backpack in transferable form are designed to remain available to the player even if the issuing game shuts down — and can be given to another player.

The intent is to put players in control of what happens to the eligible items they own. Digital items that remain on a game’s own backend continue to work exactly as they do today and can’t be transferred through Backpack.

Players who want to collect these items simply sign in to their account as usual — no seed phrase, no separate wallet setup. They cover network fees by buying XLA-NT gas credits through Xsolla Gas Station, using the payment methods they already know and prefer.

From there, players can collect eligible items they purchase or claim in their Backpack and share them with other players.

“Players should be able to share and gift digital items they own, anytime, anywhere, with anyone they know,” noted Chris Hewish, President of Xsolla (USA). “Developers gain a fresh way to monetize their games, and players gain eligible digital items that are theirs to keep. When both sides win, the games do too. We are adding options inside the tools they already use, not asking anyone to change how they work.”.

Industry observers note that when a player wants to share or give away a digital item, the transaction runs on Xsolla ZK, the blockchain network, and the network fee is paid in Xsolla Gas. This lets players hold items and pass them on to others, and it’s designed to let them carry items between supported games.

Players can cover the fee themselves in XLA or XLA-NT, while developers and partners can use XLA to pay network fees for their own item activity.

Players can cover network fees through:.

According to recent reports, more than 1,500 game teams use Xsolla (USA)’s tools and services to monetize and distribute games. Those tools are designed to work with Xsolla ZK to support the transfer of eligible digital items — and Xsolla Backpack and Xsolla Gas Station are now available without additional development for teams using compatible Xsolla (USA) products, integrating directly with existing player and payment flows.

Studios, publishers, brands, and players can learn more about Xsolla Gas Station at x.la/gas. Developers building games, wallets, marketplaces, and item services on Xsolla ZK can find network documentation, developer tools, and integration paths at xsolla.org.

Readers can also complete a short Xsolla Quest at xsolla.pro/xsolla-zk-quest to learn more about Xsolla Gas, Xsolla Gas Station, and Xsolla Backpack.

What is Xsolla Quest? Xsolla Quest lets people complete a few simple steps on an Xsolla page to receive an item.

Dogecoin co-creator Billy Markus, who goes by Shibetoshi Nakamoto on X, has weighed in on Bitcoin's potential role as an alternative to traditional retirement savings, describing Bitcoin as having the "best reason to exist.".

A 401(k) is an employer-sponsored retirement savings plan in the United States that typically allows workers to invest through a selection of financial products, often including mutual funds and exchange-traded funds.

According to recent reports, the discussion began on X as market participants reacted to the ongoing market crash, which has seen millions of dollars in liquidations in the last 24 hours. Leveraged traders took the brunt, with $1.92 billion of liquidations over 24 hours, according to CoinGlass data. Longs accounted for the majority of the damage at $1.59 billion, while short liquidations totaled $341.26 million.

Bitcoin fell to a three-month low below $63,000; Dogecoin fell to a low of $0.055, last seen in June 2023. At the time of writing, Dogecoin was down 4.63% over the last 24 hours to $0.059.

An X user commented, apparently in light of the market drop, "Cash out or crash out.".

It has been revealed that having released its latest flagship model Gemini 4 Carbon one month ago, followed by the cost-effective Gemini 4 Hydrogen, it’s now striking a balance between the two with Gemini 4 Neon. Google announced its latest artificial intelligence offering in a blog post today, saying that Neon is a general-purpose model designed to handle complex coding tasks, multistep agentic workflows and analytical reasoning.

Surprisingly, though Carbon is positioned as the tech giant’s strongest model, Neon’s performance surpassed it on some tasks, according to benchmarks the company published today. Google also said Neon completes most tasks about three times as promptly as Carbon at costs of about 60% lower, making it “competitive with the leading models in its class.”.

Here’s Google’s official benchmarks:.

Digging deeper into Google’s benchmarks, the organization said Neon outranked the midtier Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.2 Sol models on tests such as knowledge work, reasoning, automation, multimodal understanding, cybersecurity, science and math.

Those numbers were from Google’s own tests, but independent research by Artificial Analysis demonstrates that Neon achieved an impressive score of 61 on the Intelligence Index, putting it third overall, just behind Anthropic’s most powerful model, Claude Fable 5.2, which scored 65, and OpenAI’s leading model GPT-6.2 Astra, which achieved a score of 62.

Sources indicate that LAS VEGAS, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- KEENON Robotics is showcasing a lineup of commercial cleaning robots, delivery robots and the XMAN-R1 humanoid robot at ISSA Show North America 2026 in Las Vegas. The exhibit hall is open Nov. 17â19. According to IDC, KEENON ranked first worldwide in commercial service robot shipments in 2025, a position it has held for several consecutive years.

Cleaning Solutions Built for Diverse Commercial Environments.

As labor costs rise and cleaning standards become more demanding, KEENON is presenting cleaning robots for small, midsize and large facilities, with models suited to different floor types and cleaning routines.

Designed for large factories, warehouses and logistics facilities, the KLEENBOT C55 can clean up to 2,376 square meters per hour. It uses multimodal sensing to avoid obstacles autonomously in changing environments. Automatic water refilling and wastewater drainage support longer periods of continuous operation.

Recent findings suggest that for shopping centers and retail stores that need frequent floor cleaning, the KLEENBOT C40 combines sweeping and scrubbing. The KLEENBOT C30 is designed for deep carpet cleaning.

KEENON cleaning robots are at the moment deployed across more than 70 countries and regions, supporting commercial facilities worldwide.

Coordinating Multiple Robots Across Shared Spaces.

Hotels and shopping centers need floor cleaning and item delivery, and hotels may also need to move guest luggage. These tasks call for different types of robots operating in the same facility.

At ISSA Show, KEENON is showing how its cleaning robots can work alongside the S300 heavy-duty transport robot, the T11, T10 and T9 delivery robots, and the W3 hotel service robot.

KEENON is also exploring how embodied AI could support a cleaning workflow. The XMAN-R1 humanoid robot would first clear clutter and tidy tabletops. Dedicated cleaning robots such as the KLEENBOT C40 would then sweep and scrub large floor areas.

Global Deployments and North American Collaboration.

In a recent development, with 16 years of robotics experience, KEENON combines technology development with the ability to deliver, deploy and support robots worldwide. The company has shipped more than 100,000 service robots and deployed robots in more than 600 cities across over 70 countries and regions.

In a recent development, as demand for intelligent cleaning solutions grows in North America, KEENON plans to work more closely with local customers and partners. The firm plans to use its commercial deployment experience to bring embodied AI into day-to-day service operations.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. Industry observers note that chandler Fang, founder of AI payments startup t54.ai, has mentioned that the company's x402 Facilitator on the XRP Ledger (XRPL) has processed more than 10 million AI agent transactions. Fang made the comments in an interview that the XRPL Foundation published on X on November 15, and the interviewer put the number of these payments at 11.7 million.

According to Fang, XRPL had almost no transactions made by AI agents three or four months before the interview, which was recorded at XRP Seoul 2026. "The entire volume got ramped up very swiftly in the three months," he said.

According to recent reports, the x402 Facilitator works as a bridge between AI agents and payments, and agents can use XRP or the RLUSD stablecoin to move money without a separate wallet setup for every agent. Fang said that more than 200 merchants are already on the network.

According to Fang, the most common use case is paying for AI compute. Instead of paying $20 to $200 a month for an AI subscription, an agent can pay around $1 or 50 cents for a single task. "Instead, they can purchase this single compute for about $1, or 50 cents, and it can be settled on the XRPL," Fang said.

Fang mentioned that such payments have low value and high frequency, so the high throughput and low fees of XRPL give the network an advantage. He also expects agent payments to move into real-life purchases over the next few quarters. "We have the coffee shop right outside our booth, right? And we are trying to empower users to use XRP and agent payments to finish a real-life transaction," Fang said.

According to Fang, trust is the main problem for agent payments, and t54.ai's Trustline product focuses on risk management for the financial activity of AI agents. He compared the service with the chargeback feature of credit cards. "So there is no lawsuit. It is a similar experience for agents," Fang noted.

t54.ai is also part of Mastercard's agentic payment program, where the startup is responsible for risk management. The x402 Facilitator processes transactions based on Mastercard Verifiable Intent, a protocol that verifies the behavior of AI agents.

Fang stated that t54.ai, Ripple and Mastercard are in talks about a three-way collaboration, and the first results will be shown at an upcoming hackathon.

It has been revealed that "The ten million transactions are just a starting point. I think next year you should expect a lot more transactions. Maybe even more transactions settled on XRPL will be done by AI agents than by humans," Fang remarked.

Through the multiyear renewal, AT&T will continue championing U.S. Soccer and its National Teams through athlete storytelling, fan engagement and long-term investment in the sport.

Industry observers note that the renewal comes as soccer continues to gain momentum across the U.S. As more people play, watch and follow the sport across the country, AT&T and U.S. Soccer will continue creating new ways for fans to connect with the teams, athletes and moments that make soccer meaningful.

In a recent development, AT&T's support of U.S. Soccer also extends to the Arthur M. Blank U.S. Soccer National Training Center, the new home for all 27 U.S. Soccer National Teams. As a Founding Partner, AT&T will provide advanced connectivity across the campus, including AT&T Connected Fields, to support how players and coaches prepare, analyze performance and improve their game. "As soccer continues to grow, so does its ability to inspire, unite and open doors for people on and off the field. Through this partnership, we're helping more fans connect with the sport they love while supporting the athletes, programs and facilities moving the game forward.".

UPDATED 07:00 EST / NOVEMBER 19 2026.

Cybersecurity investment management company Balance Theory Inc. today revealed that it has acquired VectorBlack, a decision intelligence platform for chief information security officers developed by ThreatShare.ai, for an undisclosed sum.

Sources indicate that developed by Jason Lewis, Gerry Eaton and Wayne Schepens, VectorBlack is designed to provide CISOs with timely decision support on emerging threats, industry developments and market trends. The artificial intelligence-driven platform is aimed at anticipating the concerns most likely to catch the attention of chief executives and boards, allowing security leaders to raise them before the questions are asked.

In a recent development, rather than simply aggregating information, VectorBlack is mentioned to show security leaders what has changed in the cybersecurity landscape and why it matters to their organization. Its focus as what the company calls a CISO Strategic Intelligence Platform was shaped by input from security executives, including Ryan Clarque, CISO at Black Rifle Coffee Co. Clarque said having a strategic view ahead of a renewal, budget decision or board discussion “can make all the difference.”.

Lewis began developing the underlying technology before teaming up with Eaton, an industry analyst, and Schepens, a cybersecurity entrepreneur who founded public relations firm LaunchTech Communications in 2015.

As part of the deal, Schepens will join Balance Theory as chief cyber market analyst to help shape market strategy and product adoption. Lewis is taking on the role of principal data engineer, leading the continued development and integration of VectorBlack’s technology. Eaton will focus on applying the platform to targeted research and sector-specific intelligence for cybersecurity leaders.

At the core of Balance Theory’s offering is an AI-native platform for cybersecurity investment decisions and execution. Combining program context, proprietary market intelligence and AI agents, the platform is used by security teams to manage more than $1 billion in cybersecurity spending. It claims customers average a first-year return on investment of more than 300%.

In a recent development, vectorBlack’s technology will be integrated into the Balance Theory platform, adding to the market intelligence that already informs customer investment decisions. By tracking market developments, competitive dynamics, emerging technologies and real-world experience with security products, the combined teams are aiming to show CISOs how their own investments are performing, what others in the industry are seeing and where the market is headed.

“VectorBlack will take Balance Theory’s capabilities a step further by delivering tailored intelligence across the security product categories our customers invest in,” said Greg Baker, co-founder and chief executive of Balance Theory. “This creates a powerful new level of insight to inform smarter technology investments and long-term security strategy.”.

The company mentioned details on integration and availability will be confirmed at a later date.

Balance Theory is a venture capital-backed company that raised $19 million in a Series A round led by SYN Ventures in July, with existing investors DataTribe and the Maryland Technology Development Corp. also participating. The round coincided with Accuvant Inc. founder and former Optiv Security Inc. Chief Executive Dan Burns joining Balance Theory as executive chairman. Including a $3 million seed round in 2022, Balance Theory has raised $22 million to date.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Cryptocurrency exchange Binance has warned of the rising risk of AI scams, including the use of deepfakes that impersonate Binance executives and staff.
  • The world's largest crypto exchange recently took to X to warn its users that improvements in artificial intelligence are making it harder to distinguish fake messages from real ones.
  • "AI deepfakes are making impersonation scams harder to spot," the crypto exchange said in a post.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cryptocurrency exchange Binance has warned of the rising risk of AI scams, including the use of deepfakes that impersonate Binance executives and staff.

The world's largest crypto exchange recently took to X to warn its users that improvements in artificial intelligence are making it harder to distinguish fake messages from real ones.

"AI deepfakes are making impersonation scams harder to spot," the crypto exchange said in a post.

The cryptocurrency exchange has assured its users that no one from Binance will ever reach out to them asking for money or offering unsolicited investment advice.

Binance indicates scammers are making realistic deepfake videos featuring executives and employees of the company.

Fraudsters are using these deepfakes, some of which are very realistic, to trick potential targets through fraudulent video calls.

That way, people who fall victim to the scam might think they are interacting with real Binance personnel.

It has been revealed that binance warned that scammers often try to reach potential targets through messaging apps such as WhatsApp or Telegram. They impersonate Binance employees by using their names, photos, and job titles to appear credible.

After making contact with a potential victim, the scammer may try to convince them to send crypto, take part in an exclusive investment opportunity, or take other financial actions.

Binance has called on crypto users to be cautious about any unexpected messages they receive, even if they seem to be from someone at the firm they know.

A realistic appearance no longer guarantees a person's identity, given that AI can now easily mimic voices and facial expressions.

Users should double-check any suspicious messages through official Binance support channels before taking any action.

PORTLAND, Ore. and SAN FRANCISCO, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Dimension 6 Fitness and Beyond Power today declared a partnership bringing VOLTRA I and a curated selection of Beyond Power equipment to NikeStrength.com.

Smaller than a shoebox and weighing 13 lbs, VOLTRA I delivers up to 230 lbs of resistance and records speed, power and range of motion on every rep. Recognized by TIME, Men's Health and GQ, it is used by teams across the NBA, NFL, MLB, NHL and Premier League, and by programs in every NCAA power conference.

VOLTRA I is designed to integrate with the entire Nike Strength training equipment line. It mounts to rack uprights in seconds and moves between stations, adding cable work, variable resistance and performance data to a Nike Strength gym.

In a recent development, "Our customers are building serious gyms, and they expect every piece to earn its place," said Dimension 6 Fitness Founder Drew Conant. "Offering VOLTRA I on NikeStrength.com gives athletes another way to train with intent.".

"Together, we're helping athletes and everyday lifters get more out of their training, wherever they work out," stated Kevin Song, Vice President of Marketing at Beyond Power.

VOLTRA I and select Beyond Power equipment is now available on NikeStrength.com for customers in the United States, with additional markets to follow. The products are sold online only and are not available in stores.

About Dimension 6 FitnessBased in Portland, Oregon, Dimension 6 Fitness is a licensee of Nike with the exclusive rights to design, develop, market and distribute Nike Strength and Jordan Strength training equipment for elite and everyday athletes, from home gyms to professional facilities. Find our full catalog at nikestrength.com.

Sources indicate that about Beyond PowerFounded in 2021, Beyond Power is the sport technology company that invented VOLTRA I. It was built on the belief that resistance training has gone too long without meaningful change. Started by athletes and engineers who ran into the limits of traditional equipment firsthand, the company develops intelligent resistance systems that deliver precision, versatility and data on every rep. Its mission is to democratize advanced training methodologies, so that what was once confined to elite programs is within reach of anyone who trains. More at beyond-power.com.
